name: Ab Wheel Rollout
pro_tip: To avoid discomfort in your knees, try to avoid kneeling on a hard surface. If you want, placing a towel, blanket, or small pillow underneath your knees can ease discomfort. For more of a challenge or for more advanced lifters, you can perform this movement with your legs straight out behind you instead of on your knees.
how_to: Position yourself on your knees with your feet crossed. Hold the ab wheel roller directly under your shoulders with your arms fully extended and head facing the ground, not looking forward.
Inhale and push the ab roller forward by raising your arms and leaning forward. Make sure to keep your arms straight and keep your torso straight, squeezing your abs the entire time.
Continue rolling forward as far as you can without allowing your torso or arms to touch the floor.
Exhale and return to the starting position by bringing your arms back in towards your body. Remember to keep your torso straight and continue to squeeze your abs.

name: Air Bike
pro_tip: Do not pull on your head with your arms. Doing so can lead to later discomfort in your neck. It is best to focus on using your abs to raise you up, consciously ignoring your arms.
how_to: Lie flat on the ground with your hands behind your head, legs raised directly above your hips, and bent so that your lower leg and upper leg make a 90 degree angle.

Maintaining this angle, exhale and raise your torso with a twisting motion in the direction of your opposite knee while simultaneously drawing that knee in towards your torso. Do not bring your head forward, keep it in line with your torso.
Continue until you can no longer raise your torso with a twisting motion any longer.
Inhale and slowly return to the starting position by lowering your torso and pushing your leg away from your torso.
Switch sides and repeat the movement.

name: Alternating Straight Leg Raise
pro_tip: Breathing out more forcefully while raising your leg can increase the emphasis placed on your abdominal muscles, but is not required.
how_to: Lie on the floor in a supine position with your head facing upwards and legs fully extended.
Exhale and raise one leg up towards your body as high as you comfortably can, keeping it straight.
Continue until your leg is at least 45 degrees from the ground, but continue until your leg is pointing straight up toward the ceiling if you can.
Inhale and lower your leg back down towards the ground, continuing to keep it straight, returning to the starting position.
Switch sides and repeat the movement.

name: Arnold Press
pro_tip: This could be performed while standing to increase the involvement of core muscles, but performing it seated with a backrest is better for focusing on the development of shoulder and arm muscles. If performed seated, make sure your feet are firmly planted on the ground and your back is pressed firmly against the backrest throughout the entire movement.
how_to: Sit on a bench that has a vertical backrest while in an upright position, holding a dumbbell in each hand immediately in front of your shoulders with your palms facing towards you.
Exhale and simultaneously raise your arms overhead and to the side as you rotate your palms to face away from you.
Continue raising your arms up overhead until they are fully extended with the dumbbells directly above your shoulders.
Inhale as you lower your arms and rotate your palms towards you, returning to the starting position.

name: Around The World Superman Hold
pro_tip: You can optionally hold your arms in place for 1-2 seconds When fully outstretched in front of you and again when by your sides to increase the difficulty of the movement.
how_to: Lie on the ground in a prone position with your abdomen on the floor, arms by your side, palms facing upwards, legs raised, head up, and chest raised so that you feel as if you are squeezing your back.
Exhale and bring your arms around your body, keeping them straight while rotating your palms so that they face downwards.
Continue until your arms are fully outstretched in front of you, in front of your shoulders.
Inhale and bring your arms back around your body, rotating your palms so that you return to the starting position.

name: Assisted Dip
pro_tip: Unlike most other movements, the higher the weight you select for this movement, the easier it is to do. Some gyms have bars instead of pads. If your gym has a bar, place your feet on it instead.
how_to: With your arms fully extended, grab both handles with your palms facing inwards towards your body and place your knees on the pad.
Keeping your forearms perpendicular to the ground, inhale and lower yourself down.
Continue lowering yourself down until your upper arms are parallel with the floor.
Exhale and push yourself up until your arms are fully extended, returning to the starting position.

name: Assisted Pull Up
pro_tip: Unlike most other movements, the higher the weight you select for this movement, the easier it is to do. Some gyms have bars instead of pads. If your gym has a bar, place your feet on it instead.
how_to: With the bar in front of your nose, grab the bar slightly wider than shoulder-width apart with your palms facing away from you and place your knees on the pad.
Inhale and lower yourself down by allowing your arms to extend.
Continue lowering yourself until your arms are fully extended.
Exhale and pull on the bar to raise yourself up, returning to the starting position.

name: Assisted Straight Leg Raise
pro_tip: If you are working out at home or don't have access to a bench, any sturdy object you can hold onto that will not move can work as a replacement.
how_to: Lie on the ground next to a bench in a supine position with your head facing upwards, legs fully extended in the air, and hands holding onto a bench.
Exhale and raise your legs, keeping them straight while holding onto the bench for support.
Continue until your legs point straight up.
Inhale and lower your legs, returning to the starting position.

name: Back Extension Machine
pro_tip: Your gym may have a back extension machine with handles on the side of the seat. If it has them, hold onto them instead of crossing your arms in front of your chest.
how_to: Position yourself on the machine with your feet on the footrest and arms crossed in front of your chest.
Exhale and lean backward, extending your back. Don't allow your feet to leave the footrest.
Continue extending until your body is straight or you cannot do so any longer, whichever comes first.
Inhale and then allow yourself to bend forward, returning to the starting position.

name: Band Air Bike
pro_tip: To increase the difficulty of this movement, keep your inactive leg in the air. The band can be wrapped around any stable object if a power rack or pole is not available.
how_to: Wrap a band around a power rack or pole several inches above its lowest point.
Lie on the ground with your arms bent, feet hooked into either end of the band, and hands behind your head.
Exhale and begin to raise your torso diagonally across your body while simultaneously bringing your opposite leg up toward your chest by bending it. Do not use your arms to pull on your head.
Continue raising your torso and bringing your leg toward your chest as far as you can without allowing your lower back to leave the ground or leg to rotate.
Inhale and simultaneously lower your torso and extend your leg, returning to the starting position on the ground.
Switch sides and repeat the movement.

name: Band Calf Raise
pro_tip: You can increase the role of your traps by performing the entire movement with your shoulders shrugged, holding the shrug for the duration of the set. You should still keep your arms fully extended by your side.
how_to: Stand upright with your feet shoulder-width apart over the middle of a band, with your arms fully extended by your side and each holding one end of the band.
With your palms facing each other, exhale and raise yourself up by standing on your toes while continuing to keep your arms fully extended by your side.
Continue to raise yourself on your toes until you are no longer able to do so.
Inhale and lower yourself down until your feet are firmly planted on the ground, returning to the starting position.

name: Band Chest Fly
pro_tip: For added resistance, you can wrap the band around the power rack or pole more than once. The band can be wrapped around any stable object if a power rack or pole is not available.
how_to: Wrap a band around a power rack or pole at shoulder-level.
Stand upright your feet shoulder-width apart and in a staggered stance while grabbing each end of the band with your arms fully extended at shoulder-level and palms facing forward.
Keeping your arms fully extended and at shoulder-level, exhale and bring your arms towards each other.
Continue to bring your arms towards each other until your hands are shoulder-width apart. Avoid using your legs or torso, while simultaneously preventing your arms from bending.
Inhale and allow your arms to return to the starting position.

name: Band Chest Press
pro_tip: For added resistance, you can wrap the band around the power rack or pole more than once. The band can be wrapped around any stable object if a power rack or pole is not available.
how_to: Wrap a band around a power rack or pole at shoulder-level and stand upright.
Grab each end of the band with your arms bent perpendicularly at shoulder-level using an overhand grip.
With a staggered stance, exhale and press your arms forward and inward to extend it while simultaneously bringing them closer to the middle of your body.
Continue until your arms are fully extended while maintaining an overhand grip. Do not allow your torso or legs to assist with the movement.
Inhale and allow your arms to bend, returning to the starting position.

name: Band Cross Chest Curl
pro_tip: If you experience discomfort, you can optionally position the band at shoulder-level and perform this movement without leaning back. The band can be wrapped around any stable object if a power rack or pole is not available.
how_to: Wrap a band around a power rack or pole slightly above head level.
Stand upright with a slight backward lean while holding your arms out in front of you at shoulder-level.
Hold one end of the band in each hand, with your palms facing each other.
Exhale and bend your arms so that your hands move toward the opposite shoulder.
Continue until you are no longer able to bend your arms any further, while maintaining the position of your upper arms at shoulder-level.
Inhale and allow your arms to extend outward, returning to the starting position.

name: Band Crunch
pro_tip: If you feel discomfort, you can place a mat or towel underneath you. The band can be wrapped around any stable object if a power rack or pole is not available.
how_to: Lie on the ground with your arms fully extended over your shoulders, legs bent and your feet, legs, and back firmly planted on the ground. Wrap a band around a power rack or pole at the height of your hands.
Using an overhand grip, exhale and curl your body forward by raising your head and upper back off the ground. Maintain the position of your arms and do not allow them to help with the movement.
Continue to curl your body forward as far as you can while still keeping your lower back firmly planted on the ground, stopping lower than you would in a sit up.
While continuing to keep your arms still and at the level of your shoulders, inhale and lower your body to the ground, returning to the starting position.

name: Band Curl
pro_tip: For added benefit, hold the top position of the rep for an extra 1 second before lowering your arms to return to the starting position.
how_to: Stand upright with your feet shoulder-width apart over the middle of a band and your arms by your side holding it with an underhand grip.
Keeping your upper arm by your side, exhale and raise the band up toward your shoulder by bending your arm. Avoid using your legs or back to lift.
Continue until your arm is fully flexed and the band cannot be curled any further.
Inhale and lower the band back down, returning to the starting position.

name: Band Deep Curl
pro_tip: If you don't feel tension in the band when you start curling your arms, take a step forward. The band can be wrapped around any stable object if a power rack or pole is not available.
how_to: Wrap a band around the lowest portion of a power rack or pole.
Stand upright with a staggered stance and hold each end of the band with an underhand grip.
With your upper arms fixed behind you at a 45 degree angle, exhale and curl your arms upward by bending them towards your shoulders.
Continue until you are unable to curl your arms any further while still maintaining the position of your upper arms.
Inhale and straighten your arms, returning to the starting position.

name: Band Face Pull
pro_tip: For added resistance, you can wrap the band around the power rack or pole more than once. The band can be wrapped around any stable object if a power rack or pole is not available.
how_to: Wrap the band around a power rack or pole slightly higher than shoulder-level.
Stand upright while grabbing one end of the band in each hand with an overhand grip.
Exhale and draw your arms back towards your body, squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Continue until your arms are next to your head.
Inhale and allow your arms to extend forward, returning to the starting position.

name: Band High Curl
pro_tip: For added benefit, hold the fully bent position for an extra 1 second before allowing your arms to extend and return to the starting position. The band can be wrapped around any stable object if a power rack or pole is not available.
how_to: Wrap a band around a power rack or pole immediately below shoulder-level and stand upright with your arms outstretched in front of you at shoulder-level.
Holding each end of the band with an underhand grip, exhale and bend your arms to curl them in the direction of your shoulders. Do not allow your torso to rotate.
Maintain the position of your upper arms at shoulder-level and continue curling your arms upwards until you are no longer able to do so.
Inhale and allow your arms to extend, returning them to the starting position.

name: Band High Row
pro_tip: For added resistance, you can wrap the band around the power rack or pole more than once. The band can be wrapped around any stable object if a power rack or pole is not available.
how_to: Wrap a band around a power rack or pole slightly higher than the level of your head.
Stand upright while grabbing one end of the band in each hand, using an overhand grip.
Exhale and row your arms towards your body by driving your elbows backwards, while simultaneously squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Continue rowing until your hands are next to your chest.
Inhale and allow your arms to extend forward, returning to the starting position.

name: Band Hip Abduction
pro_tip: If you are having difficulty keeping your balance, perform the movement while positioning the inactive side of your body against a wall while still standing upright.
how_to: Stand upright with your feet shoulder-width apart over the middle of a band, with your arms shoulder-width apart and fully extended.
Grabbing the opposing end of the band with each hand, exhale and raise your leg upwards toward your side, keeping it fully extended and your torso rigid.
Continue to raise your leg until you are no longer able to raise it any further. Do not allow your torso to rotate and do not allow your arms to help with the movement.
Inhale and lower your leg, returning to the starting position.
Switch sides and repeat the movement.

name: Band Lat Pulldown
pro_tip: Bend forward further to increase the involvement of your lats. Bend forward less to increase the involvement of your rear deltoids. The band can be wrapped around any stable object if a power rack or pole is not available.
how_to: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart while bending forward and maintaining a flat back. While in this position, wrap a band around a power rack or pole at shoulder-level.
Using an overhand grip, position your arms out in front of you so that they are straight.
Exhale and bend at your arms by drawing your elbows inward toward your sides, maintaining the position of your torso.
Continue until you are unable to draw your elbows toward your sides any further without having to rotate your body.
Inhale and allow your arms to straighten, returning to the starting position.

name: Band Lying Tricep Extension
pro_tip: If you feel discomfort, you can place a mat or towel underneath you. The band can be wrapped around any stable object if a power rack or pole is not available.
how_to: Wrap a band several inches above the lowest portion of a power rack or pole and lie down with your head, back, and feet firmly planted on the floor with bent legs.
Grip one end of the band in each hand with your palms facing away from you, your upper arms directly above your shoulders, and your arms bent so that your hands are several inches from your forehead.
Exhale and extend your arms forward in front of your face while keeping your upper arm still, maintaining its position directly above your shoulders.
Continue until your arms are fully extended above your shoulders.
Inhale and allow your arms to bend, returning to the starting position.

name: Band Overhead Side Bend
pro_tip: To avoid accidentally rotating your torso, focus on keeping your belly button pointed forward. The band can be wrapped around any stable object if a power rack or pole is not available.
how_to: Stand upright with your feet shoulder-width apart and your arms fully extended overhead.  Wrap a band around a power rack or pole at the level of your hands when extended overhead.
With your arms overhead, grab the band and place one hand clasped over the other.
Exhale and bend at your side while keeping your arms directly overhead, not allowing your arms to assist with the movement.
Continue to bend at your side while maintaining the position of your arms overhead until you are no longer able to do so without rotating your torso.
Inhale and allow your torso to return to the starting position.
After all reps are completed, switch sides and repeat the movement. 10 reps prescribed means you should perform 10 reps on each side (20 total).

name: Band Overhead Tricep Extension
pro_tip: If your band is not long enough to allow you to fully extend your arms overhead, you can perform this movement by kneeling over the middle of a band instead. This will decrease ab and oblique involvement.
how_to: With your feet shoulder-width apart, step forward in a staggered stance and firmly plant your feet on the ground. Brace yourself.
With your arms raised so that your hands are directly behind your head, hold one end of the band in each hand with your palms facing away from you.
Exhale and extend your arms overhead while minimizing the movement of your upper arm.
Continue until your arms are fully extended overhead.
Inhale and lower your arms, allowing them to return to the starting position.

name: Band Preacher Curl
pro_tip: If you have difficulty balancing, try widening your stance so that you feel more stable.  Continue to keep your arms shoulder-width apart. The band can be wrapped around any stable object if a power rack or pole is not available.
how_to: Wrap a band around the lowest portion of a power rack or pole.
Squat down with your feet shoulder-width apart while holding onto each end of the band with an underhand grip.
Firmly position your upper arms shoulder-width apart on your thighs, exhale and curl the band upward towards your shoulders.
Continue curling the band upwards until you are no longer able to curl it any further while keeping your upper arms firmly positioned on your thighs.
Inhale and allow your arms to extend, returning them to the starting position.

name: Band Reverse Crunch With Hip Raise
pro_tip: If you feel discomfort, you can place a mat or towel underneath you. The band can be wrapped around any stable object if a power rack or pole is not available.
how_to: Wrap a band around a power rack or pole several inches above its lowest point.
With the band secured around your feet, lie on the floor facing the ceiling with your legs extended in front of you on the floor.
Exhale and raise your legs while curling your knees toward your head, until your thighs are directly above your hips.
Inhale briefly then exhale and kick your legs upwards while allowing your butt and lower back to come off the floor.
Continue until your legs are fully extended overhead.
Inhale and lower your legs and butt down until your butt is firmly on the ground and your legs are bent with your thighs directly above your hips.
Exhale briefly then inhale and kick your legs forward, returning to the starting position.

name: Band Reverse Fly
pro_tip: For added resistance, you can wrap the band around the power rack or pole more than once. The band can be wrapped around any stable object if a power rack or pole is not available.
how_to: Wrap two bands around the lowest portion of a power rack or two poles, with one band per pole.
With your feet shoulder-width apart, bend forward so that your back is slightly higher than parallel to the floor, grabbing a band in each hand with your palms facing each other.
While maintaining a flat back, exhale and raise your fully extended arms upwards and outwards toward your back.
Continue to raise your arms until they are at the level of your shoulders.
Inhale and lower your arms while continuing to keep them fully extended, returning to the starting position.

name: Band Split Squat Over Band
pro_tip: If your knees feel uncomfortable during this movement, try using a mat or towel, or try lowering yourself more slowly.
how_to: Stand in a lunge position with your feet shoulder-width apart.
Place one foot over the middle of a band and outstretch your other leg behind you so that your back knee makes contact with the ground.
Grip one end of the band in each hand with your palms facing each other and your  upper arms parallel to the floor.
Exhale and push your front foot into the floor to extend both legs without allowing your feet to leave the floor.
Continue until your front leg is fully extended, while preventing your arms from assisting with the movement.
Inhale and lower your body by bending your legs, returning to the starting position.
After all reps are completed, switch sides and repeat the movement. 10 reps prescribed means you should perform 10 reps on each side (20 total).

name: Band Squat Over Band
pro_tip: If you have the flexibility, squat down further until your thighs pass the point at which they are parallel to the ground.
how_to: Stand upright with your feet shoulder-width apart over the middle of a band.
Hold each end of the band with an overhand grip so that your hands are comfortably just above shoulder-level.
Inhale and break at the hip, bending your knees so that you lower yourself to the ground.
Continue lowering yourself until your thigh reaches at least parallel to the ground.
Exhale and press yourself up through your feet while keeping them firmly planted on the ground, returning to the starting position. Do not allow your arms to help with the movement.

name: Band Squat Twist
pro_tip: Look in the direction of your hands throughout the movement to limit neck discomfort. The band can be wrapped around any stable object if a power rack or pole is not available.
how_to: Squat with your feet slightly wider than shoulder-width apart and pointed slightly outwards so that your thighs are parallel to the ground or lower.
Wrap a band around a power rack or pole at the level of your shoulders while in this position.
While in a full squat position and facing perpendicularly to the band, rotate your torso to face and grasp the band with the palms of your hands clasped.
Exhale and press through your feet to stand while also rotating your torso away from the band and raising your arms diagonally upwards.
Continue until you are fully upright with your arms extended diagonally overhead.
Inhale and squat down while rotating your torso toward the band and bringing your arms diagonally downward across your body, returning to the starting position.

name: Band Tricep Kickback
pro_tip: Hold the band in place for an extra 1 second when your arms are fully extended for added benefit.
how_to: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and over the middle of a band while bending forward and maintaining a flat back.
Holding each end of the band with an underhand grip, exhale and extend your arms to straighten them out behind you.
Continue to straighten your arms until they are fully extended while making sure not to keep your upper arms and torso still.
Inhale and allow your arms to bend while keeping your upper arms in place, returning to the starting position.

name: Band Twist
pro_tip: For added resistance, you can wrap the band around the power rack or pole more than once. The band can be wrapped around any stable object if a power rack or pole is not available.
how_to: Wrap a band around a power rack or pole slightly higher than shoulder-level.
Stand upright, torso twisted, with your feet wide apart and pointed away from the band. Extend both arms in front of you and grab on end of the band with both hands.
Exhale and rotate your legs and torso while keeping your arms extended, allowing them to slightly lower to shoulder level.
Continue until you face completely forward.
Inhale and rotate back to the starting position.
After you complete all reps, switch sides and complete all reps with the other side.

name: Barbell Curl
pro_tip: If your wrists feel uncomfortable, you can substitute a regular barbell for the EZ curl bar.
how_to: Stand upright with your arms fully extended, gripping the barbell shoulder-width apart with palms facing away from you.
Keeping your upper arms by your side, exhale and raise the barbell up towards your shoulders by flexing your arms. Avoid using your legs or back to lift.
Continue until your arms are fully flexed and the barbell cannot be curled any further.
Inhale and lower the barbell back down, returning to the starting position.

name: Barbell Drag Curl
pro_tip: You can also perform this movement using an EZ curl bar if you find your wrists are uncomfortable during it.
how_to: Stand upright with your arms fully extended, gripping the barbell slightly wider than shoulder-width apart with palms facing away from you.
Exhale and raise the barbell up towards your shoulders by flexing your arms and driving your elbows backward. Avoid using your legs or back to lift.
Continue until your arms are fully flexed and the barbell cannot be curled any further.
Drive your elbows and arms forward to lift the barbell to the level of your neck.
Inhale and bring your elbows and arms backward and then down, returning the barbell to the starting position.

name: Barbell Forward Lunge
pro_tip: Try not to take too small of a step.
how_to: With feet shoulder-width apart, position yourself under the center of the barbell in the rack as you place it between your traps and upper back, and grip the barbell slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.
Lift the barbell from the rack by partially standing up and taking a step back while squeezing the barbell tightly and keeping it positioned over your upper back.
While maintaining an upright torso, take a large step forward with one foot, keeping the other foot in place.
Inhale and lower yourself to the ground by bending both legs.
Continue lowering yourself until just before your back knee comes in contact with the ground.
Exhale and push through your front foot to straighten both legs, continuing until your front leg is almost completely straight.
Take a step back returning to the starting position.
Switch sides and repeat the movement after prescribed reps are completed.

name: Barbell Front Raise
pro_tip: Make sure you do not raise the barbell above the level of your shoulder.
how_to: Stand upright with your hands in front of your shoulders, holding the barbell with an overhand grip.
Exhale and raise the barbell, keeping your arms straight. Avoid using your legs or back to lift the barbell.
Continue raising the barbell until it reaches the level of your shoulder.
Inhale and lower the barbell, returning to the starting position.

name: Barbell Glute Bridge
pro_tip: If the barbell feels uncomfortable on your hips, you can place a towel or other pad between your hips and the barbell to make the movement more pleasant.
how_to: Place a barbell on the ground and lie supine under it so that it is directly above your hips with your hands grabbing it shoulder-width apart with an overhand grip.
With knees bent, exhale and push through your heels to extend your hips and raise the barbell, keeping your head firmly on the ground the entire time.
Continue until your upper legs and torso make a straight line, holding onto the barbell tightly so that it stays in place.
Inhale and lower the barbell back down to the floor, returning to the starting position.

name: Barbell Hip Thrust
pro_tip: If the barbell feels uncomfortable on your hips, you can place a towel or other pad between your hips and the barbell to make the movement more pleasant.
how_to: Place a barbell on the ground and lie supine under it so that it is directly above your hips with your hands grabbing it shoulder-width apart with an overhand grip.
Place your upper back on a bench, while keeping your butt and feet firmly on the ground.
With knees bent, exhale and push through your heels to extend your hips and raise the barbell, keeping your upper back firmly on the bench the entire time.
Continue until your upper legs and torso make a straight line, holding onto the barbell tightly so that it stays in place.
Inhale and lower the barbell back down to the floor, returning to the starting position.

name: Barbell Preacher Curl
pro_tip: If your wrists feel uncomfortable, you can substitute a regular barbell for the EZ curl bar.
how_to: Sit down with your arms fully extended, gripping the barbell shoulder-width apart with palms facing away from you.
Keeping your upper arms pressed to the pad, feet on the floor, and butt on the bench, exhale and raise the barbell up towards your shoulders by flexing your arms.
Continue until your arms are fully flexed and the barbell cannot be curled any further.
Inhale and lower the barbell back down, returning to the starting position.

name: Barbell Reverse Curl
pro_tip: Keep your wrists up for the best effect, don't let them drop.
how_to: Stand upright with your arms fully extended, gripping the barbell shoulder-width apart with an overhand grip.
Keeping your upper arms by your side, exhale and raise the barbell up towards your shoulders by flexing your arms. Avoid using your legs or back to lift.
Continue until your arms are fully flexed and the barbell cannot be curled any further.
Inhale and lower the barbell back down, returning to the starting position.

name: Barbell Reverse Wrist Curl
pro_tip: This movement will benefit from you performing it slowly, try to drag out the length of each rep by lowering the barbell back down slowly each time.
how_to: Sit on the bench with your feet firmly planted on the ground, forearms rested on your thighs, and the barbell held with an overhand grip.
Allow your hands to fully bend downward, letting the barbell hang in front of you.
Exhale and raise only your hands, lifting the barbell.
Continue raising your hands and the barbell until you no longer can do so.
Inhale and lower your hands and the barbell, returning to the starting position.

name: Barbell Shoulder Press
pro_tip: If you feel discomfort in your lower back during this movement, you may be leaning too far backward. Try to maintain an upright torso throughout the entire movement. If you struggle with this, squeezing your glutes and abs can help.
how_to: Standing upright, position yourself under the barbell so that you may grab it slightly wider than shoulder-width apart with your palms facing away from you.
Remove the barbell from the rack and take a step backward.
Exhale and raise your arms up overhead, pushing up in a straight line, without hitting your chin.
Continue raising your arms up overhead until they are fully extended with the barbell directly overhead.
Inhale and lower the barbell, returning to the starting position.
After all reps are completed, return the barbell to the rack.

name: Barbell Split Squat
pro_tip: Try to keep your toes pointed forward.
how_to: With feet shoulder-width apart, position yourself under the center of the barbell in the rack as you place it between your traps and upper back, and grip the barbell slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.
Lift the barbell from the rack by partially standing up and taking a step back while squeezing the barbell tightly and keeping it positioned over your upper back.
While maintaining an upright torso, take a moderate step forward with one foot, keeping the other foot in place.
Inhale and lower yourself to the ground by bending both legs.
Continue lowering yourself until just before your back knee comes in contact with the ground.
Exhale and push through your front foot to straighten both legs, continuing until your front leg is almost completely straight, returning to the starting position.
After all reps are completed, switch sides and repeat the movement, then return the barbell to the rack.

name: Barbell Split Squat On Bench
pro_tip: If squatting down feels awkward, adjust the distance of the bench behind you by moving it.
how_to: With feet shoulder-width apart, position yourself under the center of the barbell in the rack as you place it between your traps and upper back, and grip the barbell slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.
Lift the barbell from the rack by standing up and taking a step back while squeezing the barbell tightly and keeping it over your upper back.
While maintaining an upright torso, lift one leg so that it is placed behind you on a bench, resting the top of your foot on the bench.
Inhale and lower your body by allowing both legs to bend.
Continue to lower your body until your front thigh is at least parallel to the ground.
Exhale and push through your front foot while keeping it flat on the floor to stand upright, returning to the starting position.
After all reps are completed, switch sides and repeat the movement, then return the barbell to the rack.

name: Barbell Sumo Deadlift
pro_tip: Grip the barbell very tightly.
how_to: Place a barbell on the floor and position yourself over the center of it with your feet much wider than shoulder-width apart and shins about 1 inch away from the barbell.
Maintaining a straight back, bend down with your legs while leaning forward and position your hands on the barbell shoulder-width apart with one palm facing each direction and fully extended arms.
Exhale and push through your feet while extending your legs to begin lifting the barbell while maintaining a flat back.

After the barbell passes your knees, drive through your hips while continuing to extend your legs until you are standing fully upright with your torso in line with the rest of your body. Do not lean further back than this.
Inhale and begin to lower the barbell by bending your legs and lowering your torso while focusing on maintaining a flat back above all else.
Rest the barbell on the floor for 1 second before beginning your next rep.

name: Battle Ropes
pro_tip: To decrease the difficulty, shorten the ropes by wrapping them around the pole multiple times.
how_to: Wrap the battle ropes around a pole, leaving a similar length of rope free on either side.
Squat down and grab one end of the battle ropes with each hand.
While maintaining a straight back and not moving your legs, swing one arm up while you swing the other down.
Continue for the desired duration, breathing regularly.

name: Bench Dip
pro_tip: If you want to make the movement easier, try bringing your feet a little closer to the rest of your body and bending your legs slightly more.
how_to: Place your hands on a bench shoulder-width apart with your feet fully extended in front of you.
Inhale and lower yourself towards the ground by letting your arm flex and bend downwards, while keeping your torso straight.
Continue until your upper arm is just above parallel to the ground.
Exhale and extend your arm until it is completely straight to raise your body, returning to the starting position.

name: Bench Press
pro_tip: By having a spotter help you unrack the bar at the start of the lift, you will have an easier time during the rest of the lift. Just make sure you don't let them touch the barbell once you start benching unless you need help racking the barbell.
how_to: Lie flat on the bench so that your head, upper back, lower back, and both feet are firmly pressed against the bench and ground at all points.
Grab the barbell on the rack at slightly wider than shoulder-width by extending your arms and bring it forward until it is over the middle of your chest and your arms are fully extended.
Inhale and lower the barbell towards the middle of your chest.
Continue lowering the barbell until just before it makes contact with your chest.
Exhale and push the barbell upwards returning to the starting position, while keeping your feet, lower back, upper back, and head firmly planted.
After all reps are completed, return the barbell to the rack.

name: Bench Tricep Extension
pro_tip: To make this exercise easier, you can bring your feet closer towards the bench and allow your knees to bend.
how_to: Position your hands shoulder-width apart on a bench with palms facing away from you and your feet fully extended behind you.
While maintaining a straight torso, inhale and lower yourself by allowing your elbow to come down and arms to bend.
Continue until your head is several inches from the bench.
Exhale and push through your hands to extend your arms and return to the starting position.

name: Bent Knee Inverted Row
pro_tip: You can raise or lower the bar on the smith machine to adjust the difficulty. The higher the position, the easier this movement is.
how_to: Position yourself underneath the bar grabbing it with an overhand grip wider than shoulder-width and placing your feet out in front of you with your knees bent so that your thighs are parallel to the ground.
Exhale and row yourself towards the bar while allowing your knees to extend to aid you.
Continue until your upper chest can no longer get closer to the bar.
Inhale and lower yourself, returning to the starting position with arms fully extended.

name: Bent Over Row
pro_tip: You can change the focus of this exercise slightly by changing up where you grip the barbell. Wider grips will favor the back muscles more while narrower grips will favor the biceps more. Just don't grab the barbell closer than shoulder-width.
how_to: Place a barbell on the floor and approach it with your shins several inches away.

Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, grab the barbell with your arms fully extended and hands just outside of shoulder-width and pick it up, lifting to a point where your knees are moderately bent and your torso is leaning forward.
Maintaining a flat back and keeping your chest up, exhale and pull the barbell toward your upper abdomen while squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Continue to pull until just before the bar touches your upper abdomen without allowing your torso or legs to change position.
Inhale and lower the barbell down to the starting position with your arms fully extended.

name: Bodyweight Squat
pro_tip: If you have the flexibility, squat down further until your thighs pass the point at which they are parallel to the ground.
how_to: Stand upright with your feet shoulder-width apart and pointed slightly outwards while your arms are extended and raised in front of you at your shoulder level.
Inhale and break at the hip, bending your knees so that you lower yourself to the ground.
Continue lowering yourself until your thigh reaches at least parallel to the ground.
Exhale and press yourself up through your feet while keeping them firmly planted on the ground, returning to the starting position.

name: Cable Assisted Nordic Leg Curl
pro_tip: The higher the weight you use is, the easier this movement will be.
how_to: Place your knees on the seat of a lat pulldown machine while securing your feet underneath the footrest and grabbing the lat pulldown bar with a wider than shoulder-width overhand grip.
Inhale and allow your knees to extend, lowering your body while keeping your torso straight.
Continue lowering yourself until your torso is almost parallel to the floor.
Exhale and drive your heels back into the pad while leaning back, returning to the starting position while maintaining a straight torso.

name: Cable Chest Press
pro_tip: If the handles you use are uncomfortable, try switching them out for similar ones with a different grip.
how_to: Standing upright, grab one cable with each hand with an overhand grip and position them at your shoulder level.
Exhale and press your arms forwards and inwards, bringing them towards each other.
Continue until your arms are fully extended.
Inhale and allow your elbows to be driven backward, returning to the starting position.

name: Cable Crossover Reverse Fly
pro_tip: If the handles you use are uncomfortable, try switching them out for similar ones with a different grip.
how_to: Bend forward maintaining a straight torso and grab the cable on either side of you with your opposing hand.
Exhale and raise your arms out and back behind you while keeping them straight and fully extended.
Squeeze your shoulder blades together and continue raising your arms until they reach shoulder level.
Inhale and lower your arms back down, returning to the starting position.

name: Cable Crossover Row
pro_tip: If the handles you use are uncomfortable, try switching them out for similar ones with a different grip.
how_to: Stand upright and grab the cable on either side of you with your opposing hand.
Exhale and lower your arms back towards your body, tucking your elbows in towards your sides and squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Continue until your elbows pass behind your back.
Inhale and allow your elbows to extend and arms to raise, returning to the starting position.

name: Cable Curl With Curl Bar
pro_tip: If a curved curl bar like the one animated makes your wrists feel uncomfortable, substitute it for a straight bar attachment instead.
how_to: Stand upright with your arms fully extended, gripping the bar shoulder-width apart where the bar curves inward with palms facing away from you.
Keeping your upper arms by your side, exhale and raise the bar up towards your shoulders by flexing your arms. Avoid using your legs or back to lift.
Continue until your arms are fully flexed and the bar cannot be curled any further.
Inhale and lower the bar back down, returning to the starting position.

name: Cable Curl With Lat Bar
pro_tip: Focus on squeezing the biceps consciously throughout the entire movement for the greatest effect.
how_to: Stand upright with your arms fully extended, gripping the bar shoulder-width apart with palms facing away from you.
Keeping your upper arms by your side, exhale and raise the bar up towards your shoulders by flexing your arms. Avoid using your legs or back to lift.
Continue until your arms are fully flexed and the bar cannot be curled any further.
Inhale and lower the bar back down, returning to the starting position.

name: Cable Deadlift
pro_tip: This movement cannot be performed on machines where the cables are far apart.
how_to: Maintaining a straight back, bend down with your legs while leaning forward, and grab each handle by your side with fully extended arms so that the cables are next to your midfoot.
Exhale and push through your feet while extending your legs to begin lifting the cables while maintaining a flat back.

After the cable passes your knees, drive through your hips while continuing to extend your legs until you are standing fully upright with your torso in line with the rest of your body. Do not lean further back than this.
Inhale and begin to lower the cable by bending your legs and lowering your torso while focusing on maintaining a flat back above all else.
Returning to the starting position, rest the cables in the bottom position for 1 second before beginning your next rep.

name: Cable Front Raise
pro_tip: Make sure you do not raise the bar above the level of your shoulder.
how_to: Stand upright with your hands in front of your shoulders, holding the bar with an overhand grip.
Exhale and raise the bar, keeping your arms straight. Avoid using your legs or back to lift the bar.
Continue raising the bar until it reaches the level of your shoulder.
Inhale and lower the bar, returning to the starting position.

name: Cable Hip Adduction
pro_tip: If you don't have the attachment shown in the video, you can always improvise with a regular pulley handle, but it is not ideal.
how_to: Stand upright adjacent to a cable machine, with your attached leg raised and a hand holding onto the pole for support.
With your other leg firmly planted on the ground, exhale and bring your attached leg in towards your planted leg.
Continue until your attached leg passes your grounded leg, keeping the attached leg straight.
Inhale and allow your attached leg to move away from your body, returning to the starting position.
After all reps are completed, switch sides and repeat the movement. 10 reps prescribed means you should perform 10 reps on each side (20 total).

name: Cable Hip Adduction
pro_tip: If you don't have the attachment shown in the video, you can always improvise with a regular pulley handle, but it is not ideal.
how_to: Stand upright adjacent to a cable machine, with your attached leg raised and a hand holding onto the pole for support.
With your other leg firmly planted on the ground, exhale and bring your attached leg in towards your planted leg.
Continue until your attached leg passes your grounded leg, keeping the attached leg straight.
Inhale and allow your attached leg to move away from your body, returning to the starting position.
After all reps are completed, switch sides and repeat the movement. 10 reps prescribed means you should perform 10 reps on each side (20 total).

name: Cable Hip Extension
pro_tip: If you don't have the attachment shown in the video, you can always improvise with a regular pulley handle, but it is not ideal.
how_to: Standing upright, hold onto the pole with one leg attached to the machine.
Exhale and extend your leg behind you while keeping it straight.
Continue until you can no longer extend it further behind you without moving your torso.
Inhale and bring your leg forward, allowing it to return to the starting position.
After all reps are completed, switch sides and repeat the movement. 10 reps prescribed means you should perform 10 reps on each side (20 total).

name: Cable Lateral Raise
pro_tip: For greater benefit, try holding the cables for 1 second before lowering them when your arms are parallel to the ground.
how_to: Stand upright and grab the cable on either side of you with your opposing hand, holding them with a neutral grip.
With your arms straight, exhale and raise them out to your sides.
Keeping your arms straight, continue to raise your arms until they are parallel with the ground.
Inhale and lower your arms back down, returning them to the starting position.

name: Cable Lying Chest Fly
pro_tip: Consciously focus on squeezing your chest at the point where your hands are about to meet for added benefit.
how_to: Lie flat on the bench so that your head, upper back, lower back, and both feet are firmly pressed against the bench and ground at all points.
Grabbing each handle with your arms extended to your sides and at shoulder level, exhale and bring your arms up and in towards each other.
Continue bringing your arms together until just before they meet.
Inhale and lower your arms down to your sides, stopping when they are parallel to the ground and returning to the starting position.

name: Cable Oblique Crunch
pro_tip: The higher the cable attachment you use, the harder this exercise will be.
how_to: Stand upright with your feet shoulder-width apart and pointed away from the pole. Grab the cable with both hands and arms extended in front of you above your shoulder level.
Exhale and rotate your torso and legs while keeping your arms straight, driving them down and across your body.
Continue until your hands reach the level of your opposite thigh.
Inhale and rotate your torso up and back, returning to the starting position.
After all reps are completed, switch sides and repeat the movement. 10 reps prescribed means you should perform 10 reps on each side (20 total).

name: Cable Push Down
pro_tip: Try to consciously squeeze your triceps at the bottom for added benefit.
how_to: Stand upright, gripping the bar overhand and holding it at chest level.
Exhale and extend your arms downward while keeping your torso straight and not allowing it or your upper arms to move.
Continue pressing down until your arms are fully extended.
Inhale and return to the starting position by allowing your arm to bend upwards again.

name: Cable Rope Curl
pro_tip: Focus on squeezing the biceps consciously throughout the entire movement for the greatest effect.
how_to: Stand upright, gripping one edge of the rope with each hand using a neutral grip.
Keeping your upper arms by your side, exhale and raise the rope up towards your shoulders by flexing your arms. Avoid using your legs or back to lift.
Continue until your arms are fully flexed and the rope cannot be curled any further.
Inhale and lower the rope back down, returning to the starting position.

name: Cable Row
pro_tip: Depending on your gym, the machine available to you may have separate footrests instead of a single plate.
how_to: Sit on the bench with your feet positioned on the footrest, gripping the handle at the level of your upper abdomen with an upright torso.
Exhale and drive your elbows back, bringing your hands towards your upper abdomen while simultaneously squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Continue until your elbows pass your torso.
Inhale and allow your arms to extend, returning to the starting position while your shoulder blades part.

name: Cable Row
pro_tip: If you experience discomfort in your back, perform this movement without moving your torso and instead only move your arms and shoulder blades.
how_to: Sit on the bench, leaning forward with your feet placed on the footrests and hands gripping the bar with palms facing each other.
Exhale and lean backward while maintaining a straight torso and driving your elbows toward your back at the level of your abdomen, tucking them in.
Continue while simultaneously squeezing your shoulder blades together until your elbows pass your torso.
Inhale and lean forward allowing your arms to extend and shoulder blades to part, returning to the starting position.

name: Cable Row With Lat Bar
pro_tip: Try to avoid moving your head while pulling.
how_to: Sit down with your feet planted on the footrests and grab the bar slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.
Exhale and drive your arms back towards your body, tucking your elbows in towards your sides and squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Continue until your elbows pass behind your back.
Inhale and allow your elbows to extend and arms to raise, returning to the starting position while your shoulder blades part.

name: Cable Seated Crunch
pro_tip: You can optionally sit in the middle of the bench instead of the end if it is more comfortable for you.
how_to: Sit on a bench holding a rope overhead with both hands.
Exhale and bend your torso forward.
Continue until your elbows pass your thighs.
Inhale and raise your torso up, returning to the starting position.

name: Cable Seated Rear Lateral Raise
pro_tip: Try to not bend forward too far, you want to be at about 45 degrees during this movement.
how_to: Sit on the bench with your torso bent moderately forward, grabbing each handle with the opposing hand.
Exhale and raise your arms up in the direction of your upper back and shoulders with a shrugging motion, while keeping them straight.
Continue raising your arms until they are parallel to the floor.
Inhale and allow your arms to lower down, returning to the starting position.

name: Cable Shoulder Press
pro_tip: If you feel discomfort in your lower back during this movement, you may be leaning too far backward. Try to maintain an upright torso throughout the entire movement. If you struggle with this, squeezing your glutes and abs can help.
how_to: Stand with one cable in each hand positioned at shoulder level and palms facing away from you.
Exhale and raise your arms up overhead, pushing up in a straight line.
Continue raising your arms up overhead until they are fully extended with your hands directly overhead.
Inhale and lower your arms back down, returning to the starting position.

name: Cable Shrug
pro_tip: This movement will benefit from you performing it slowly, try to drag out the length of each rep by lowering the barbell back down slowly each time.
how_to: Stand upright, holding the bar slightly less than shoulder-width apart with an overhand grip.
Keeping your arms straight, exhale and raise your shoulders with a shrugging motion to lift the bar.
Continue to raise the bar until you are no longer able to lift it through shrugging alone.
Inhale and lower the bar, returning to the starting position.

name: Cable Side Bend
pro_tip: Do your best to prevent yourself from leaning forward or back, do not twist your torso at all. Just lower yourself down to the side.
how_to: Stand upright while gripping the handle and holding it by your side with a fully extended arm.
Inhale and lower yourself down to the opposite side by bending your torso.
Continue until you are no longer able to lower yourself through exclusively bending to the side.
Exhale and raise yourself up to return to the starting position.
After all reps are completed, switch sides and repeat the movement. 10 reps prescribed means you should perform 10 reps on each side (20 total).

name: Cable Twist
pro_tip: The lower the cable attachment you use, the harder this exercise will be.
how_to: Stand upright with your feet shoulder-width apart and pointed towards the pole. Grab the cable with both hands and arms extended in front of you at your hip level.
Exhale and rotate your torso and legs while keeping your arms straight, driving them up and across your body.
Continue until your hands pass above your head.
Inhale and rotate back to the starting position.
After all reps are completed, switch sides and repeat the movement. 10 reps prescribed means you should perform 10 reps on each side (20 total).

name: Cable Underhand Tricep Pushdown
pro_tip: Focus on consciously squeezing your triceps while you press down for added benefit.
how_to: Stand upright with your upper arms by your sides and hands gripping the bar at your shoulder level with an underhand shoulder-width apart grip.
Exhale and press the bar down by extending your arms, while keeping your upper arms in place.
Continue lowering the bar until your arms are straight.
Inhale and allow the bar to pull your arms up, bending them and returning to the starting position.

name: Cable Upright Row
pro_tip: If a certain bar or handle feels uncomfortable for you, you can always switch it out for another one.
how_to: Stand upright holding the bar in front of you with a greater than shoulder-width overhand grip.
Exhale and shrug your shoulders while driving your elbows upwards.
Continue to drive your elbows upwards until the bar passes your lower chest.
Inhale and lower the bar, returning it to the starting position.

name: Calf Raise Machine
pro_tip: To increase the effectiveness of this exercise, lower yourself down slowly during each rep.
how_to: Sit on the machine with your hands on the handles and the front of your feet on the footrests so that only the balls of your feet and toes are in contact with them.
Exhale and press through the balls of your feet and toes to raise your legs and the machine up.
Continue until you cannot bring your feet up any further.
Inhale and lower your feet, returning to the starting position.

name: Chair Calf Raise
pro_tip: If you can't find a chair, holding onto other sturdy objects of a similar height may help.
how_to: Stand upright on a block while holding onto the back of a chair.
Exhale and stand up on your toes, focusing on maintaining balance while keeping your legs straight.
Continue raising yourself until you can't stand any higher on your toes.
Inhale and lower yourself back down, returning to the starting position.

name: Chair Dip
pro_tip: If chairs are unavailable, try to replace them with other stable objects of a similar height.
how_to: Position yourself between two chairs with your hands facing inwards towards each other.
Raise yourself up so that your arms are fully extended, keeping your legs crossed.
Inhale and lower yourself down towards the ground by bending at the elbows.
Continue lowering yourself until your upper arms are parallel to the ground.
Exhale and push yourself up until your arms are straight again, returning to the starting position.

name: Chair Inverted Row
pro_tip: If chairs are unavailable, try to replace them with other stable objects of a similar height.
how_to: Place a bar between two chairs.
Position yourself underneath the bar grabbing it with an overhand grip wider than shoulder-width and placing your feet out in front of you with your legs straight.
Exhale and row yourself towards the bar, squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Continue until your upper chest makes contact with the bar.
Inhale and lower yourself, returning to the starting position.

name: Chair Pull Up
pro_tip: As you get stronger, try to decrease the amount you extend at your knees.
how_to: Place a bar between two chairs.
Sitting upright, position yourself underneath the bar grabbing it, and an overhand grip wider than shoulder-width and placing your feet out in front of you with your knees bent.
With arms extended overhead, exhale and pull yourself up toward the bar, extending your knees to help you.
Continue until your chin passes the bar.
Inhale and lower yourself down until your arms are extended, returning to the starting position.

name: Chest Dip
pro_tip: Some chest dip stations have multiple hand grip settings, pick one and stick with it.
how_to: With your arms fully extended, grab both handles with your palms facing inwards towards your body.
Keeping your forearms perpendicular to the ground, inhale and lower yourself down.
Continue lowering yourself down until your upper arms are parallel with the floor.
Exhale and push yourself up until your arms are fully extended, returning to the starting position.

name: Chest Fly Machine
pro_tip: Try to momentarily squeeze your chest consciously when your hands are close together for added benefit.
how_to: Sit on the machine with arms fully extended in line with your torso at the level of the middle of your chest.
Exhale and bring your arms together while keeping them straight.
Continue bringing your arms together until your hands are about 1 inch from each other.
Inhale and bring your arms back to your sides, returning to the starting position.

name: Chest Press Machine
pro_tip: Grip the handles further apart to emphasize your chest more, or closer together to emphasize your triceps more.
how_to: Sit on the machine with your feet firmly planted on the ground and head pressed against the backrest, holding the handles with an overhand grip at chest level.
Exhale and press your arms forward and upward.
Continue pressing your arms forward until they are fully extended.
Inhale and bring your arms back, returning to the starting position.

name: Chin Up
pro_tip: Try to tighten your abs consciously to prevent your body from swinging during this movement.
how_to: Grab the bar shoulder-width apart with your palms facing towards you and hold yourself up so that your arms are almost fully extended.
Exhale and pull yourself up by driving your elbows back and tucking them into your sides.
Continue pulling yourself up while simultaneously bringing your shoulder blades down and back until your chin passes the bar.
Inhale and then lower yourself down, returning to the starting position.

name: Clap Push Up
pro_tip: If you cannot leave the ground by pushing as hard as you can, you are not strong enough to perform this movement yet.
how_to: Position yourself on the ground with legs fully extended and hands shoulder-width apart at the level of your chest.
Exhale and forcefully press yourself up by extending your arms.
Continue pressing as hard as you can so that you leave the ground.

Upon leaving the ground, inhale and clap your hands together before quickly returning them to the push up position. Keep your head shrugged back to protect your face in case you can't catch yourself in time.
Catch yourself with your hands and lower yourself down, returning to the starting position.

name: Close Grip Band High Row
pro_tip: For added resistance, you can wrap the band around the power rack or pole more than once. The band can be wrapped around any stable object if a power rack or pole is not available.
how_to: Wrap a band around a power rack or pole slightly higher than the level of your head.
Stand upright while grabbing one end of the band in each hand with an overhand grip.
Exhale and row your arms towards your body by driving your elbows backwards and simultaneously tucking them in toward your sides.
Continue rowing until your hands are next to your chest, while simultaneously squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Inhale and allow your arms to extend forward, returning to the starting position.

name: Close Grip Band Row
pro_tip: For added resistance, you can wrap the band around the power rack or pole more than once. The band can be wrapped around any stable object if a power rack or pole is not available.
how_to: Wrap a band around a power rack or pole at shoulder-level.
Stand upright while grabbing one end of the band in each hand using an overhand grip.
Exhale and row your arms towards your abdomen by driving your elbows backwards and tucking them in toward your sides.
Continue rowing until your hands are next to your chest, while simultaneously squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Inhale and allow your arms to extend forward, returning to the starting position.

name: Close Grip Barbell Bench Press
pro_tip: If you want to increase the emphasis on your triceps, try tucking your elbows into your sides throughout the entire movement.
how_to: Lie flat on the bench so that your head, upper back, lower back, and both feet are firmly pressed against the bench and ground at all points.
Grab the barbell on the rack slightly inside of shoulder-width by extending your arms and bring it forward until it is over the middle of your chest and your arms are fully extended.
Inhale and lower the barbell towards the middle of your chest.
Continue lowering the barbell until just before it makes contact with your chest.
Exhale and push the barbell upwards returning to the starting position, while keeping your feet, lower back, upper back, and head firmly planted.
After all reps are completed, return the barbell to the rack.

name: Close Grip Dumbbell Bench Press
pro_tip: Focus on keeping your elbows tucked in, it's easy to accidentally let them rotate outwards.
how_to: Lie flat on the bench so that your head, upper back, lower back, and both feet are firmly pressed against the bench and ground at all points while holding two dumbbells at your chest with your palms facing each other.
Exhale and push the dumbbells straight up, keeping your elbows tucked in.
Continue pushing the dumbbells up until your arms are fully extended.
Inhale and bring your arms back down, returning them to the starting position.

name: Close Grip Lat Pulldown
pro_tip: Make sure the pad tightly secures your thighs, if it's too loose you'll have a hard time staying on the bench.
how_to: Sit down with your feet firmly planted on the ground and thighs secured into place by the pad, while gripping the bar overhead with an underhand grip shoulder-width apart.
Exhale and drive your elbows downwards towards the ground, while pulling your shoulder blades down and back.
Continue to pull the bar down until your elbows are in line with your torso and shoulder blades are fully pulled back.
Inhale and allow your arms to raise overhead while parting your shoulder blades, returning to the starting position.

name: Close Grip Push Up
pro_tip: Focus on squeezing your triceps as you push up for added benefit.
how_to: Position yourself on the ground with legs fully extended and hands closer than shoulder-width apart at the level of your chest.
Exhale and forcefully press yourself up by extending your arms.
Continue pressing up until your arms are fully extended, preventing your hips from sagging.
Inhale and lower yourself to the ground, returning to the starting position.

name: Cobra Push Up
pro_tip: Try to explode up at the points where you push yourself up in this movement.
how_to: Position yourself on the ground with legs fully extended and hands slightly wider than shoulder-width apart at the level of your chest.
Inhale and lower yourself towards the floor by leaning forward and allowing your elbows to bend.
As your chest almost touches the ground, arch your back upwards and begin to push up through your hands, exhaling.
Continue to arch backward and push through your hands until your arms are fully extended.
Inhale and begin lowering yourself while bending forward until your chest almost touches the ground.
Exhale and push forward with your hands to rock yourself back into the starting position.

name: Cocoon
pro_tip: Try not to strain your neck too much while crunching forward.
how_to: Lie on the ground in a supine position with your arms extended overhead and legs straight out in front of you.
Exhale and bring your torso and arms up towards your thighs while simultaneously driving your knees towards your chest and bending your legs.
Continue until you can grab your shins, hugging your legs.
Inhale and extend your torso, arms, and legs, returning to the starting position.

name: Cross Body Hammer Curl
pro_tip: Squeeze your biceps as you curl the dumbbell upwards for added benefit.
how_to: Stand upright with your hands by the side of your body with palms facing inwards, holding one dumbbell in each hand with a neutral grip.

Keeping your upper arm by your side, exhale and raise one dumbbell up towards your opposite shoulder by flexing your arm and maintaining a neutral grip. Avoid using your legs or back to lift the dumbbell.
Continue until your arm is fully flexed and the dumbbell cannot be curled any further.
Inhale and lower the dumbbell back down, returning to the starting position.
Switch sides and repeat the movement.

name: Crunch
pro_tip: Avoid pulling on your head with your hands as it can lead to discomfort in the neck area later on.
how_to: Lie on a mat or on the floor with your knees bent. Position your hands so that they are interlocked behind your head.
Exhale and raise your chest up while keeping your lower back on the ground.
Continue to raise your chest up as far as you can while still keeping your lower back on the ground, stopping lower than you would in a sit up.
Inhale and lower yourself back down slowly, returning to the starting position.

name: Crunch Machine
pro_tip: Exhale deeply as you crunch down to further activate your abs.
how_to: Sit on the machine with your arms crossed in front of you.
Exhale and crunch your body forwards, while keeping your feet and butt firmly in place.
Continue to crunch forward until the pad is just above thigh level.
Inhale and allow yourself to raise your torso back up, returning to the starting position.

name: Deadlift
pro_tip: Grip the barbell tightly.
how_to: Place a barbell on the floor and position yourself over the center of it with your feet shoulder-width apart and shins about 1 inch away from the barbell.
Maintaining a straight back, bend down with your legs while leaning forward and position your hands on the barbell shoulder-width apart with an overhand grip and fully extended arms.
Exhale and push through your feet while extending your legs to begin lifting the barbell while maintaining a flat back.

After the barbell passes your knees, drive through your hips while continuing to extend your legs until you are standing fully upright with your torso in line with the rest of your body. Do not lean further back than this.
Inhale and begin to lower the barbell by bending your legs and lowering your torso while focusing on maintaining a flat back above all else.
Returning to the starting position, rest the barbell on the floor for 1 second before beginning your next rep.

name: Decline Barbell Bench Press
pro_tip: By having a spotter help you unrack the barbell at the start of the lift, you will have an easier time during the rest of the lift. Just make sure you don't let them touch the barbell once you start benching unless you need help racking the bar.
how_to: Lie flat on the bench so that your head, upper back, and lower back are firmly pressed against the bench and ground at all points, with your feet secured by the pad.
Grab the barbell on the rack at slightly wider than shoulder-width by extending your arms and bring it forward until it is over the middle of your chest with your arms fully extended.
Inhale and lower the barbell towards the middle of your chest.
Continue lowering the barbell until just before it makes contact with your chest.
Exhale and push the barbell upwards returning to the starting position, while keeping your feet, lower back, upper back, and head firmly planted.
After completing all reps, return the barbell to the rack.

name: Decline Barbell Pullover
pro_tip: Try to avoid bringing the barbell too far back behind your head, if your shoulders feel uncomfortable it's best to start with the barbell a little higher up.
how_to: Lie flat on the bench so that your head, upper back, and lower back are firmly pressed against the bench and ground at all points, with your feet secured by the pad.
Holding the barbell overhead with a shoulder-width overhand grip and arms fully extended, inhale and lower the barbell behind your head by lowering your arms backward.
Continue while keeping your arms straight until the barbell passes your head.
Exhale and raise the barbell up until it reaches chest level, returning to the starting position.

name: Decline Crunch
pro_tip: Avoid pulling on your head with your hands because it can lead to discomfort in the neck area later on.
how_to: Lie on a decline bench with your legs secured on the end. Position your hands so they are interlocked behind your head. This is the starting position.
Exhale and raise your chest up while keeping your lower back on the bench.
Continue to raise your chest up as far as you can while still keeping your lower back on the bench, stopping lower than you would in a sit up.
Inhale and lower yourself back down slowly, returning to the starting position.

name: Decline Dumbbell Bench Press
pro_tip: You can adjust the angle of the bench to change the difficulty of this movement.
how_to: Lie flat on the bench so that your head, upper back, and lower back are firmly pressed against the bench and ground at all points, with your feet secured by the pad.
Holding one dumbbell in each hand with an overhand grip at the level of your chest, exhale and push both of your hands up and towards each other.
Continue pushing until your arms are fully extended and just before the dumbbells meet.
Inhale and lower the dumbbells back down to the starting position.

name: Decline Dumbbell Chest Fly
pro_tip: For added benefit, squeeze your chest tightly while bringing the dumbbells together.
how_to: Lie flat on the bench so that your head, upper back, and lower back are firmly pressed against the bench and ground at all points, with your feet secured by the pad.
Hold one dumbbell in each hand at shoulder level with your arms fully outstretched to your sides and palms facing up.
Exhale and bring your arms together.
Continue bringing your arms together until your hands are about 1 inch from each other.
Inhale and lower the dumbbells until you return to the starting position.

name: Decline Push Up
pro_tip: To make this movement easier, place your feet on a table or bench rather than pressed against a wall.
how_to: Position your hands on the ground at shoulder level, slightly wider than shoulder-width apart, and press your feet up against a wall with straight legs to hold yourself in place.
While maintaining a straight torso, exhale and allow your arms to extend, raising yourself up.
Continue until your arms are fully extended.
Inhale and lower yourself to the ground until just before your chest makes contact with the ground, continuing to maintain a rigid torso and returning to the starting position.

name: Decline Twist
pro_tip: Avoid pulling on your head with your hands as it can lead to discomfort in the neck area later on.
how_to: Lie on a decline bench with your legs secured on the end. Position your hands so they are interlocked behind your head.
Exhale and raise your torso up, rotating so that your elbow moves towards your opposite knee.
Continue to raise yourself until just before your elbow touches your knee.
Inhale and lower yourself back down, returning to the starting position.
Switch sides and repeat the movement.

name: Diamond Push Up
pro_tip: Focus on squeezing your triceps as you push up for added benefit.
how_to: Position yourself on the ground with legs fully extended and hands in a diamond position at the level of your chest.
Exhale and forcefully press yourself up by extending your arms.
Continue pressing up until your arms are fully extended, preventing your hips from sagging.
Inhale and lower yourself to the ground, returning to the starting position.

name: Dumbbell Backwards Lunge
pro_tip: Focus on maintaining balance above all else.
how_to: Stand upright with feet shoulder-width apart and a dumbbell in each hand by your side with palms facing inward.
While maintaining an upright torso, take a large step backward with one foot, keeping the other foot in place.
Inhale and lower your torso to the ground by bending both legs.
Continue lowering yourself until just before your back knee comes in contact with the ground.
Exhale and push through your front foot to straighten both legs, continuing until your front leg is almost completely straight.
Take a step forward, returning to the starting position.
After all reps are completed, switch sides and repeat the movement. 10 reps prescribed means you should perform 10 reps on each side (20 total).

name: Dumbbell Bench
pro_tip: If you want to emphasize your triceps more, tuck your elbows in. Leave them flared out to focus more on your chest.
how_to: Lie flat on the bench so that your head, upper back, lower back, and both feet are firmly pressed against the bench and ground at all points while holding two dumbbells at shoulder level with an overhand grip.
Exhale and push both of your hands up and towards each other.
Exhale as you squeeze your chest and push the dumbbells up until your arms are fully extended.
Continue pushing until your arms are fully extended and just before the dumbbells meet.
Inhale and return the dumbbells back down to the starting position.

name: Dumbbell Burpee
pro_tip: As you get stronger, try to jump higher.
how_to: Stand upright with feet shoulder-width apart and a dumbbell in each hand by your sides, with palms facing inward.
Inhale and break at your hips, sitting down and allowing your torso to come slightly forward while keeping it straight.
Once the dumbbells pass your knees, lean forward with a straight back to place them on the ground.
While continuing to hold onto the dumbbells exhale push off with your feet so that your legs are straight behind you.
Inhale and jump forward to a squatting position while holding onto the dumbbells.
Exhale and squat up while maintaining a flat back, pushing up as hard as you can so that you jump.
Land, returning to the starting position.

name: Dumbbell Calf Raise
pro_tip: Balance is important in this movement, focus on it consciously to limit the risk of falling.
how_to: While standing on a block or raised platform on the edge of your toes, hold two dumbbells by your sides.
Exhale and raise yourself off the floor by standing on your toes.
Continue raising yourself until you can no longer raise yourself up through solely your toes any longer.
Inhale and lower yourself back down to the starting position.

name: Dumbbell Concentration Curl
pro_tip: Consciously squeeze your bicep while curling the dumbbell up for added benefit.
how_to: Sitting on a bench while leaning forward, hold one dumbbell in your hand with an underhand grip, resting your elbow on your thigh.
Keeping your elbow on your thigh, exhale and raise the dumbbell up towards your shoulder by flexing your arm.
Continue until the dumbbell reaches shoulder level.
Inhale while continuing to keep your elbow on your thigh and lower the dumbbell, returning it to the starting position.
After all reps are completed, switch sides and repeat the movement. 10 reps prescribed means you should perform 10 reps on each side (20 total).

name: Dumbbell Curl
pro_tip: Squeeze your biceps consciously while curling up for added benefit.
how_to: Stand upright with your hands by the side of your body with palms facing inwards, holding one dumbbell in each hand with a neutral grip.

Keeping your upper arms by your side, exhale and raise the dumbbells up towards your shoulders by flexing your arms and simultaneously rotating your palms inward so that your palms are facing you. Avoid using your legs or back.
Continue until your arms are fully flexed and the dumbbells cannot be curled any further.
Inhale and lower your arms back down, returning to the starting position.

name: Dumbbell Fly
pro_tip: For added benefit, squeeze your chest consciously as you bring your arms together.
how_to: Lie flat on the bench so that your head, upper back, lower back, and both feet are firmly pressed against the bench and ground at all points.
Hold one dumbbell in each hand at shoulder level with your arms fully outstretched to your sides and palms facing up.
Exhale and bring your arms together.
Continue bringing your arms together until your hands are about 1 inch from each other.
Inhale and lower the dumbbells until you return to the starting position.

name: Dumbbell Goblet Squat
pro_tip: Focus your attention on holding the dumbbell in place because it can be difficult to maintain your grip during this movement.
how_to: Stand upright with a shoulder-width stance holding a single dumbbell at chest level with both palms facing inwards.
Inhale and break at your hips, sitting down and allowing your torso to come slightly forward while keeping it straight.
Continue until your thighs are at least parallel to the floor.
Exhale and push through your heels, returning to the starting position.

name: Dumbbell High Shrug
pro_tip: For added benefit, lower the dumbbells slowly while lowering them.
how_to: Stand upright with one dumbbell in each hand and palms facing inward.
Exhale and shrug your shoulders while driving your elbows upwards and keeping the dumbbells at your sides.
Continue until the dumbbells reach the middle of your abdomen.
Inhale and lower the dumbbells, returning to the starting position.
