name: Dumbbell Iron Cross
pro_tip: Do not allow the dumbbells to drop below your shoulder level.
how_to: Squat down with your arms extended in front of you at shoulder level with a neutral grip and torso upright.
Exhale and push through your heels to stand up while swinging your arms around towards your back.
Continue until you are standing upright with your arms fully extended out to your sides.
Inhale and bring your arms forward towards each other while squatting down, returning to the starting position.

name: Dumbbell Overhead Tricep Extension
pro_tip: Try to keep your elbows pointed forward throughout the movement for the greatest effect.
how_to: Stand upright holding a single dumbbell behind your head with both hands, with both arms flexed.
Exhale and extend your arms upwards to raise the dumbbell overhead.
Continue until your arms are fully extended overhead and straight, making sure you do not allow your upper arm to move.
Inhale and then lower the dumbbell, returning to the starting position.

name: Dumbbell Pullover
pro_tip: Pay careful attention to your grip on the dumbbell, it is easy to accidentally drop if you are not paying attention.
how_to: Lie flat on the bench so that your upper back is rested on the bench, with your feet in front of you and thighs parallel to the ground.
Holding a single dumbbell behind your head with bent arms, exhale and raise your arms forward towards your chest while extending your arms.
Continue until the dumbbell is centered over your chest, while maintaining the position of your legs.
Inhale and then lower the dumbbell back down behind your head, returning to the starting position.

name: Dumbbell Pylo Squat
pro_tip: Depending on the length of your arms, you may not be able to squat down low enough. If you can't squat until your thighs are parallel to the ground, hold the dumbbell up a little higher.
how_to: Stand upright with a wider than shoulder-width stance while holding a single dumbbell with both hands while your arms are fully extended out in front of you.
Inhale with your feet pointed outwards and break at your hips, sitting down and maintaining an upright torso.
Continue lowering yourself until your thighs are at least parallel to the floor.
Exhale and push through your heels, returning to the starting position.

name: Dumbbell Reverse Curl
pro_tip: Keep your wrists up for the best effect, don't let them drop.
how_to: Stand upright with feet shoulder-width apart and holding two dumbbells in front of your body with an overhand grip.
Keeping your upper arms by your side, exhale and raise the dumbbells up towards your shoulders by flexing your arms. Avoid using your legs or back to lift.
Continue until your arms are fully flexed and the dumbbells cannot be curled any further.
Inhale and lower the dumbbells to return to the starting position.

name: Dumbbell Romanian Deadlift
pro_tip: Do not lean back further than a neutral standing position because doing so can cause injury.
how_to: Stand upright and grab two dumbbells with an overhand grip and pick them up with arms fully extended and in front of your body.
Inhale and lower your body by bending forward while maintaining a flat back and minimizing bending at your knees.
Continue bending forward with a flat back until the dumbbells pass your knees.
Exhale and stand upright by leaning back, focusing on maintaining a flat back to return to the starting position.

name: Dumbbell Row
pro_tip: If a bench is not available, substitute it for another flat and sturdy surface that you are sure can support your body weight.
how_to: Lean on the bench with your leg and a fully extended arm while holding a dumbbell in your other arm underneath your shoulder with an inward facing grip.
Exhale and drive your elbow backward, keeping your torso and other arm from moving.
Continue driving your elbow backward to lift the dumbbell until your elbow passes your torso.
Inhale and lower the dumbbell, straightening out your arm to return to the starting position.
After all reps are completed, switch sides and repeat the movement. 10 reps prescribed means you should perform 10 reps on each side (20 total).

name: Dumbbell Seesaw Press
pro_tip: If you experience neck discomfort this movement can be performed without moving your head and only leaning your torso slightly to the side.
how_to: Stand upright while holding a dumbbell in each hand immediately in front of your shoulders with your palms facing each other.
Maintaining your neutral grip, exhale extending one arm overhead while turning your head to look up at it and slightly leaning to the side.
Continue to extend your arm until it is fully extended overhead.
Inhale and lower your arm, returning to the starting position.
Switch sides and repeat the movement.

name: Dumbbell Shoulder Press
pro_tip: This could be performed while standing to increase the involvement of core muscles, but performing it seated with a backrest is better for focusing on shoulder and arm muscles. If performed seated, make sure your feet are firmly planted on the ground and your back is pressed firmly against the backrest throughout the entire movement.
how_to: Sit on a bench that has a vertical backrest while in an upright position, holding a dumbbell in each hand with your arms at shoulder level and to the side and palms facing forward.
Exhale, extending your arms both up and in.
Continue pressing up and in until your arms are fully extended.
Inhale and lower the dumbbells, returning to the starting position.

name: Dumbbell Squat
pro_tip: If you can, try to avoid allowing the dumbbells to touch the floor.
how_to: Stand upright with a shoulder-width stance, holding dumbbells by your sides with palms facing inward and arms fully extended.
Inhale and break at your hips, sitting down and allowing your torso to bend moderately forward.
Continue until your thighs are at least parallel to the floor.
Exhale and push through your heels, returning to the starting position.

name: Dumbbell Stiff Legged Deadlift
pro_tip: If you aren't flexible enough to lower the dumbbells past your knees while maintaining a straight back and legs, lower them a shorter distance until your flexibility improves.
how_to: Stand upright and grab two dumbbells with an overhand grip and pick them up with arms fully extended and in front of your body.
Inhale and lower your body by bending forward while maintaining a flat back and straight legs.
Continue bending forward with a flat back until the dumbbells pass your knees.
Exhale and stand upright by leaning back, focusing on maintaining a flat back and straight legs to return to the starting position.

name: Dumbbell Sumo Deadlift
pro_tip: Do not lean back further than a neutral standing position because doing so can cause injury.
how_to: Place a dumbbell on its side and approach it with a wider than shoulder-width stance and toes pointed slightly outwards.
Grab the dumbbell with both hands while squatting down with a flat back, keeping it in the center of your body.
Exhale and stand up by extending your knees and leaning back, focusing on maintaining a flat back.
Continue until you are standing completely upright.
Inhale and lower yourself down while maintaining a flat back to return to the starting position.

name: Dumbbell Tricep Kickback
pro_tip: Hold the dumbbells in place for an extra 1 second when your arms are fully extended for added benefit.
how_to: While bending forward and maintaining a flat back, hold two dumbbells with your palms facing each other and drive your elbows past your back.
While keeping your upper arms in place tucked into your sides, exhale and extend your arms to push the dumbbells up and back behind you.
Continue pushing the dumbbells until your arms are straight while making sure to not move your torso.
Inhale and lower the dumbbells while continuing to keep your upper arms in place, returning to the starting position.

name: Elbow To Knee Crunch
pro_tip: Try not to pull on your head with your hand because it can lead to neck discomfort down the line.
how_to: Lie supine on the floor with one leg bent, the other resting across your thigh, and the opposite hand behind your head.
Exhale and raise your chest up from the side of your hand in the direction of the raised leg.
Continue until your elbow touches your knee.
Inhale and lower yourself down to the starting position.
After all reps are completed, switch sides and repeat the movement. 10 reps prescribed means you should perform 10 reps on each side (20 total).

name: Elbow To Knee Sit Up
pro_tip: Lower yourself down slowly for an added benefit.
how_to: Lie supine on the floor with bent knees and your hands clasped in front of you.
Exhale and raise your chest up, twisting your torso towards the opposite leg.
Continue until your elbow touches your knee.
Inhale and lower yourself down to the starting position.
Switch sides and repeat the movement.

name: Elliptical
pro_tip: This is a low impact version of cardio that is at low risk of agitating your knee.
how_to: Position yourself on the machine by placing both feet on the pedals and grabbing both handles.
Select the appropriate settings on the machine for your planned cardio.
Press start.
Rhythmically move one arm and its opposite leg forward at the same time your other arm and leg move backward.

name: EZ Bar Bench Press
pro_tip: To emphasize your chest more, flare your elbows out. To focus more on your triceps, keep your elbows more tucked in.
how_to: Lie flat on the bench so that your head, upper back, lower back, and both feet are firmly pressed against the bench and ground at all points.
Grab the EZ bar on the rack slightly inside of shoulder-width by extending your arms and bring it forward until it is over the middle of your chest and your arms are fully extended.
Inhale and lower the EZ bar towards the middle of your chest.
Continue lowering the EZ bar until just before it makes contact with your chest.
Exhale and push the EZ bar upwards returning to the starting position, while keeping your feet, lower back, upper back, and head firmly planted.
Once all reps are completed, return the EZ bar to the rack.

name: EZ Bar Concentration Curl
pro_tip: If you do not have access to an EZ bar, you can substitute the EZ bar for a standard barbell.
how_to: Sit upright with your arms fully extended in front of your thighs, gripping the EZ bar closer than shoulder-width apart with palms facing away from you.
Keeping your elbows pressed into your thighs, exhale and raise the EZ bar up towards your shoulders by flexing your arms.
Continue until your arms are fully flexed and the EZ bar cannot be curled any further.
Inhale and lower the EZ bar down while continuing to keep your elbows pressed into your thighs, returning to the starting position.

name: EZ Bar Pullover
pro_tip: Try to avoid bringing the EZ bar too far back behind your head, if your shoulders feel uncomfortable it's best to start with the EZ bar a little higher up.
how_to: Lie flat on the bench so that your head, upper back, lower back, and both feet are firmly pressed against the bench and ground at all points.
Position the EZ bar behind and slightly below your head with your elbows bent and palms facing away from you.
Exhale and raise your upper arm over your body, keeping your elbow bent.
Continue to bring your upper arm over your body until the EZ bar is directly over your chest.
Inhale and bring the EZ bar back over your head, lowering it down and returning to the starting position.

name: EZ Bar Reverse Curl
pro_tip: Do not allow your wrists to drop while lifting the EZ bar, keep them stiff.
how_to: Stand upright with your arms fully extended, gripping the EZ bar shoulder-width apart with an overhand grip.
Keeping your upper arms by your side, exhale and raise the EZ bar up towards your shoulders by flexing your arms. Avoid using your legs or back to lift.
Continue until your arms are fully flexed and the EZ bar cannot be curled any further.
Inhale and lower the EZ bar back down, returning to the starting position.

name: EZ Bar Upright Row
pro_tip: This movement can also be performed with a regular barbell if an EZ bar is not available.
how_to: Stand upright, holding an EZ bar shoulder-width apart with an overhand grip.
Keeping your arms straight, exhale and raise your shoulders with a shrugging motion while driving your elbows upwards to lift the EZ bar.
Continue raising the EZ bar until it reaches your lower chest.
Inhale and lower the EZ bar, returning to the starting position.

name: Floor Tricep Dips
pro_tip: If you want to increase your range of motion, start with your butt raised higher up.
how_to: Sit on the ground with your knees bent, butt raised off the ground, and hands behind you, directly under your shoulders.
Exhale and allow your legs to extend, raising yourself up.
Continue to raise yourself until your arms are completely straight while keeping your butt up.
Inhale and bend your arms, lowering yourself until just before your butt makes contact with the ground, returning to the starting position.

name: Flutter Kick
pro_tip: Rhythmically breathe during this movement, inhaling whenever one leg reaches the highest point and exhaling when that same leg reaches the lowest point every time.
how_to: Lie face down on a bench so that the end of the bench is directly under your hips and your legs are held straight out behind you.
While holding onto the bench firmly with your hands, raise one straight leg while lowering the other.
Continue raising one leg and lowering the other until you can no longer do so while your abdomen stays pressed against the bench.
Return each leg back to its starting position then repeat with the other side.

name: Forearm Push Up
pro_tip: If this movement is too difficult, you can perform it on your knees instead.
how_to: Lie prone on the floor with your hands positioned shoulder-width apart under your neck, and legs extended straight behind you.
With your forearms resting on the floor and elbows tucked in pointing behind you, exhale and press yourself up, extending your arms.
Continue until your arms are fully extended, making sure to keep your torso in line with your lower body.
Inhale and lower yourself down, while keeping your elbows tucked in, returning to the starting position with your forearms on the floor.

name: Frog Crunch
pro_tip: Try not to pull on your head with your hands because it can lead to neck discomfort down the line.
how_to: Lie supine on the floor with your hands behind your head, knees pointed outwards, and feet pressed against one another.
Exhale and raise your chest up while simultaneously bringing your thighs up and towards your chest.
Continue until your knees are several inches from your thighs.
Inhale, lowering your legs and torso to return to the starting position.

name: Front Foot Elevated Goblet Split Squat
pro_tip: You can get creative with what you use to elevate your foot. As long as it is a flat elevated surface and is stable, meaning it will not move, it can work.
how_to: Stand upright with a shoulder-width stance holding a single dumbbell at chest level with both palms facing inwards.
While maintaining an upright torso, take a moderate box forward onto a step with one foot, keeping the other foot in place.
Inhale and lower yourself to the ground by bending both legs.
Continue lowering yourself until just before your back knee comes in contact with the ground.
Exhale and push through your front foot to straighten both legs, continuing until your front leg is almost completely straight, returning to the starting position.
After all reps are completed, switch sides and repeat the movement. 10 reps prescribed means you should perform 10 reps on each side (20 total).

name: Front Raise
pro_tip: You can optionally hold both dumbbells in place for 1 second when it is at the highest point for added training. Doing this too often can fatigue you faster so only do it occasionally. Just make sure to not go above shoulder height or hold them for longer than 1 second.
how_to: Stand upright with your hands in front of your shoulders, holding a dumbbell in each hand with an overhand grip.
Exhale and raise both dumbbells, keeping your arms straight. Avoid using your legs or back to lift.
Continue raising the dumbbells until they reach the level of your shoulder.
Inhale and lower your arms, returning to the starting position.

name: Front Squat
pro_tip: If using a heavy weight with this movement, protect your wrists by resting the barbell on your front shoulders and driving your elbows upwards to allow your hands to hold it there.
how_to: With feet shoulder-width apart, position yourself under the center of the barbell in the rack as you grip the barbell in front of you slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.
Lift the barbell from the rack by partially standing up and taking a step back while squeezing the bar tightly, keeping your wrists tight and firmly in place.
Inhale and break at your hips, sitting down and keeping your torso upright.
Continue until your thighs are at least parallel to the floor.
Exhale and push through your heels to return to the starting position.
After all reps are completed, walk forward to return the barbell to the rack.

name: Front Squat With Crossed Arms
pro_tip: Focus on keeping your elbows up and torso upright more than anything else. Doing so can prevent the barbell from falling forward.
how_to: With feet shoulder-width apart, position yourself under the center of the barbell in the rack as you rest it on your upper shoulders.
Cross your arms over the top of the barbell and grip it with both hands to secure in place over your shoulders.
Lift the barbell from the rack by partially standing up and taking a step back while keeping your elbows up to prevent the barbell from falling.
Inhale and break at your hips, sitting down and keeping your torso upright.
Continue until your thighs are at least parallel to the floor.
Exhale and push through your heels to return to the starting position.
After all reps are completed, walk forward to return the barbell to the rack.

name: Glute Kickback Machine
pro_tip: Some machines may have a pad for your active leg to push instead of a bar.
how_to: Stand on the machine with one leg rested underneath your body and the other leg on the bar.
While holding onto the machine's handles for stability, exhale and extend the leg you placed on the bar back behind you.
Continue extending your leg until it is straight.
Inhale and draw your leg in forward, returning to the starting position.
After all reps are completed, switch sides and repeat the movement. 10 reps prescribed means you should perform 10 reps on each side (20 total).

name: Hack Squat Machine
pro_tip: Keep your feet flat on the floor of the machine, do not allow them to raise.
how_to: Stand on the machine with your legs fully extended and the pads rested on top of your shoulders.
With your legs shoulder-width apart and while holding onto the handles, exhale and lower your body by breaking at the hips.
Continue until your thighs are at least parallel with the floor of the machine.
Inhale and push through your feet to stand back up, returning to the starting position.

name: Hammer Curl
pro_tip: Squeeze your biceps as you curl the dumbbells upwards for added benefit.
how_to: Stand upright with your hands by the side of your body with palms facing inwards, holding one dumbbell in each hand with a neutral grip.
Keeping your upper arms by your side, exhale and raise the dumbbells towards your shoulders by flexing your arm and maintaining a neutral grip. Avoid using your legs or back to lift the dumbbell.
Continue until your arms are fully flexed and the dumbbells cannot be curled any further.
Inhale and lower the dumbbells back down, returning to the starting position.

name: Hanging Knee Tuck
pro_tip: Try to avoid moving your arms or upper body at all during this movement.
how_to: Grab the bar overhead with an overhand grip wider than shoulder-width apart, maintaining fully extended arms and straight legs.
Exhale and raise your legs up, gradually tucking them in as they approach your chest.
Continue to raise and tuck in your legs until they reach the level of your lower chest.
Inhale and lower your legs, returning to the starting position.

name: Hanging Oblique Knee Tuck
pro_tip: Try to avoid moving your arms or upper body at all during this movement.
how_to: Grab the bar overhead with an overhand grip wider than shoulder-width apart, maintaining fully extended arms and straight legs.
Exhale and raise your legs towards one side, tucking them in as you raise them.
Continue until your legs pass your upper abdomen.
Inhale and lower your legs, returning to the starting position.
Switch sides.

name: Hanging Straight Leg Raise
pro_tip: Inhale and lower your legs, returning to the starting position.
how_to: Grab the bar overhead with an overhand grip wider than shoulder-width apart, maintaining fully extended arms and straight legs.
Exhale and raise your legs, keeping them straight.
Continue to raise your legs until you cannot do so any longer.
Try to avoid moving your arms or upper body at all during this movement.

name: Heel Touch Lateral Lunge
pro_tip: As your flexibility increases, you should be able to step further away from your body.
how_to: Stand upright with your feet shoulder-width apart and hands by your sides.
Inhale, lifting one leg and straighten it out to the side as far as you can while simultaneously bending down to touch your heel.
Continue until you touch your heel and your foot is planted on the ground.
Exhale and stand up while bringing your leg back in towards your body, returning to the starting position.
Switch sides.

name: High Band Chest Press
pro_tip: For added resistance, you can wrap the band around the power rack or pole more than once. The band can be wrapped around any stable object if a power rack or pole is not available.
how_to: Wrap a band around a power rack or pole 1-2 feet above head level and stand upright.
Grab each end of the band with your arms bent perpendicularly at shoulder-level using an overhand grip.
With a staggered stance, exhale and press both arms forward, downward, and inward to extend them while simultaneously bringing them closer to the middle of your body.
Continue until your arms are fully extended. Do not allow your torso or legs to assist with the movement.
Inhale and allow your arms to raise and bend, returning to the starting position.

name: High Cable Chest Fly
pro_tip: Squeeze your chest while driving your arms forward and down for added benefit.
how_to: Stand between two cables positioned above shoulder level, gripping them with your palms facing forward.
Exhale and bring your arms forward and down, keeping them straight.
Continue until just before your hands would touch.
Inhale and allow your arms to raise, returning to the starting position.

name: High Row Machine
pro_tip: If needed adjust the pad or seat height so that your thighs are properly secured.
how_to: Sit on the machine with your feet firmly planted on the ground, thighs secured by the pad, and hands placed on the handles.
Exhale and drive your elbows down and backward, flexing your arms while simultaneously squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Continue until your elbows are by your sides.
Inhale and allow your arms to raise and extend while simultaneously parting your shoulder blades, returning to the starting position.

name: Hip Abduction Machine
pro_tip: To maximize benefits, make sure the machine is set up so that your legs start close together.
how_to: Sit on the machine while gripping the handles by your sides.
Exhale and push your thighs outwards while keeping your butt firmly planted in the seat.
Continue until you can no longer do so.
Inhale and draw your thighs back towards the center of your body, returning to the starting position.

name: Hip Adduction Machine
pro_tip: To maximize benefits, make sure the machine is set up so that your legs start far apart.
how_to: Sit on the machine while gripping the handles by your sides.
Exhale and push your thighs inwards while keeping your butt firmly planted in the seat.
Continue until the pads are just about to touch.
Inhale and draw your thighs back outwards, returning to the starting position.

name: Hip Thrust
pro_tip: Try not to use your hands to push yourself up. Only use your lower body.
how_to: Place your upper back on a bench, while keeping your butt and feet firmly on the ground.
With knees bent, exhale and push through your heels to extend your hips and raise your butt, keeping your upper back firmly on the ground the entire time.
Continue until your upper legs and torso make a straight line.
Inhale and lower yourself back down to the ground, returning to the starting position.

name: Hyperextension
pro_tip: Make sure your feet are tightly secured behind you to avoid accidentally falling.
how_to: Position yourself so that your feet are firmly held in place by the pads and your hips are in line with the end of the platform.
Inhale and lower yourself down by bending your torso forward while your arms are crossed over your chest.
Continue until you are almost upside down, keeping your back flat.
Exhale and extend backward, leaning back until your torso is in line with your lower body, returning to the starting position.

name: Incline Barbell Row
pro_tip: If your bench has too high of an incline, you may not be able to pick up the barbell to start the movement. Aim for an incline around 45º. Ask a friend for help handing it off for you if needed.
how_to: Position yourself prone on an incline bench, with your legs extended behind you and arms extended just below shoulder level.

Using an overhand grip greater than shoulder-width apart, pick up the barbell and exhale, rowing it towards your chest by driving your elbows out and backward, squeezing your shoulder blades together to do so.
Continue to drive your elbows back and pull your shoulder blades together until your elbows are by your sides.
Inhale and lower the barbell down, returning it to the starting position.

name: Incline Bench
pro_tip: Select an incline between 30º-45º and stick with it. The higher the incline, the more you'll train your shoulder muscles.
how_to: Lie flat on a bench so that your head, upper back, lower back, and both feet are firmly pressed against the bench and ground at all points.
Grab the barbell on the rack at slightly wider than shoulder-width by extending your arms and bring it forward until it is over your upper chest and your arms are fully extended.
Inhale and lower the barbell towards your upper chest.
Continue lowering the barbell until just before it makes contact with your chest.
Exhale and push the barbell upwards returning to the starting position, while keeping your feet, lower back, upper back, and head firmly planted.
After all reps are completed, return the barbell to the rack.

name: Incline Chest Press Machine
pro_tip: For best results, try to set up the machine so that your hands don't start far away from your chest or shoulders.
how_to: Sit in the machine so that your hands are positioned just in front of your shoulders, with your feet, lower back, and head all firmly planted in place.
Exhale, extending your arms up and inward.
Continue until your arms are fully extended overhead.
Inhale and lower your arms, returning to the starting position.

name: Incline Dumbbell Curl
pro_tip: Select an incline between 30º-45º and stick with it. The higher the incline, the more you'll train the long head of your biceps.
how_to: Lie flat on the bench so that your head, upper back, lower back, and both feet are firmly pressed against the bench and ground at all points while holding two dumbbells at your sides with a neutral grip.
Keeping your upper arm by your side, exhale and raise both dumbbells up towards your shoulders by flexing your arms and simultaneously rotating your palm inward so that your palm is facing you.
Continue until your arms are fully flexed and the dumbbells cannot be curled any further.
Inhale and lower the dumbbells down, returning to the starting position.

name: Incline Dumbbell Fly
pro_tip: Select an incline between 30º-45º and stick with it. The higher the incline, the more you'll train your shoulder muscles.
how_to: Lie flat on the bench so that your head, upper back, lower back, and both feet are firmly pressed against the bench and ground at all points while holding two dumbbells at shoulder level with an overhand grip.
Hold one dumbbell in each hand at shoulder level with your arms fully outstretched to your sides and palms facing up.
Exhale and bring your arms together.
Continue bringing your arms together until your hands are about 1 inch from each other.
Inhale and lower the dumbbells until you return to the starting position.

name: Incline Dumbbell Front Raise
pro_tip: Select an incline between 30º-45º and stick with it. The higher the incline, the more you'll train your shoulder muscles.
how_to: Lie flat on the bench so that your head, upper back, lower back, and both feet are firmly pressed against the bench and ground at all points while holding two dumbbells in front of you with an overhand grip and arms extended.
Exhale and raise the dumbbells up towards your head, while keeping your arms straight.
Continue until your arms are diagonal at a 45º angle with the ground.
Inhale and lower the dumbbells down, remembering to keep your arms fully extended, returning to the starting position.

name: Incline Dumbbell Press
pro_tip: Select an incline between 30º-45º and stick with it. The higher the incline, the more you'll train your shoulder muscles.
how_to: Lie flat on the bench so that your head, upper back, lower back, and both feet are firmly pressed against the bench and ground at all points while holding two dumbbells at shoulder level with an overhand grip.
Exhale and press through both hands to raise the dumbbells up and towards each other.
Continue until your arms are fully extended.
Inhale and lower your arms, returning to the starting position.

name: Incline Hammer Curl
pro_tip: Select an incline between 30º-45º and stick with it. The higher the incline, the more you'll train the long head of your biceps.
how_to: Lie flat on the bench so that your head, upper back, lower back, and both feet are firmly pressed against the bench and ground at all points while holding two dumbbells at your sides with a neutral grip.
Keeping your upper arm by your side, exhale and raise both dumbbells up towards your shoulders by flexing your arms.
Continue until your arms are fully flexed and the dumbbells cannot be curled any further.
Inhale and lower the dumbbells down, returning to the starting position.

name: Incline Reverse Crunch
pro_tip: Avoid pulling on your head with your hands as it can lead to discomfort in the neck area later on.
how_to: Lie flat on the bench so that your head, upper back, and lower back are firmly pressed against the bench and your arms are holding onto the bench.
With knees bent, exhale and draw your thighs in towards your chest, allowing your butt to come off of the bench.
Continue until your knees are just about to make contact with your upper chest.
Inhale and lower your legs, returning them to the starting position.

name: Incline Straight Leg Raise
pro_tip: The higher the incline, the harder the movement will be.
how_to: Lie flat on the bench so that your head, upper back, and lower back are firmly pressed against the bench and your arms are holding onto the bench.
With legs straight, exhale and draw your thighs in towards your chest, allowing your butt to come off of the bench.
Continue raising your legs until they are pointed straight up.
Inhale and lower your legs, returning to the starting position.

name: Inverted Row
pro_tip: To make this movement easier, increase the height of the bar. To make it harder, lower it.
how_to: Position yourself underneath the bar grabbing it with a shoulder-width overhand grip and placing your feet out in front of you with your legs straight.
Exhale and row yourself towards the bar, squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Continue until just before your upper chest makes contact with the bar.
Inhale and lower yourself down, returning to the starting position.

name: Jump Lunge
pro_tip: This movement is high impact, so take extra care to avoid your knee accidentally making contact with the ground.
how_to: With your feet shoulder-width apart, take a moderate step backward and squat down to the point just before your back knee touches the ground.
Raise the arm on the side of your back leg forward, and bring your other arm backward.
Exhale and push through your front foot as hard as you can so that it pushes your front leg backward. Simultaneously, drive your back knee forward, making sure to keep your torso upright.
Inhale and land, catching yourself in a lunging position with legs reversed.
Switch sides and repeat the movement.

name: Jump Sprinter Lunge
pro_tip: This movement is high impact, so take extra care to avoid your knee accidentally making contact with the ground.
how_to: With your feet shoulder-width apart, take a large step backward and squat down to the point just before your back knee touches the ground while leaning forward so that your hands touch the ground in front of you.
Exhale and push through your front foot as hard as you can so that it pushes your front leg backward. Simultaneously, drive your back knee forward, maintaining the position of your torso.
Inhale and land, catching yourself in a lunging position with legs reversed and your hands on the ground in front of you.
Switch sides and repeat the movement.

name: Jump Squat
how_to: Stand upright with your feet shoulder-width apart and pointed slightly outward.
Inhale and break at your hips, sitting down and keeping your torso upright.
Continue until your thighs are at least parallel to the ground.
Exhale and forcefully push through your feet to stand up, extending your legs.
Just before your legs are completely extended, push as hard as you can through your feet to jump up off of the ground.
Land to catch yourself, returning to the starting position.

name: Kettlebell Angled Press
pro_tip: If a kettlebell is unavailable, this movement can be performed with a single dumbbell.
how_to: Bend forward with a straight back until your torso is almost parallel to the ground while holding a kettlebell immediately in front of your chest.
Exhale and raise the dumbbell diagonally overhead by extending your arms, focusing on keeping them up.
Continue until your arms are fully extended.
Inhale and return your arms back towards your body by driving your elbows back while keeping the kettlebell close to your torso, returning the kettlebell to the starting position.

name: Kettlebell Halo
pro_tip: A kettlebell is preferable, but if you only have a light dumbbell, you can use that as well.
how_to: Stand upright with your shoulders wider than shoulder-width apart, holding a kettlebell behind your head with bent arms.
Exhale and rotate the kettlebell around your body, bringing it to the front of your chest.
Holding the kettlebell in front of your chest, inhale.
Exhale, raising the kettlebell, and rotating it behind your back to return it to the starting position.
Switch directions and repeat the movement.

name: Kettlebell Seesaw Press
pro_tip: If you experience neck discomfort this movement can be performed without moving your head and only leaning your torso slightly to the side.
how_to: Stand upright while holding a kettlebell in each hand immediately in front of your shoulders with your palms facing each other.
Maintaining your neutral grip, exhale extending one arm overhead while turning your head to look up at it and slightly leaning to the side.
Continue to raise your arm until it is fully extended overhead.
Inhale and lower your arm, returning to the starting position.
Switch sides and repeat the movement.

name: Knee Tuck
pro_tip: To make the movement more difficult, you can keep your feet raised in between reps, keeping them from touching the ground.
how_to: Lie supine on the ground with your legs bent, arms by your sides, and head firmly planted on the ground.
Exhale and raise your knees towards your face while keeping your legs bent, allowing your butt and lower back to leave the ground.
Continue to raise your legs until you can no longer do so while still keeping your upper back on the ground.
Inhale and lower your legs to the ground, returning to the starting position.

name: Kneeling Band Crunch
pro_tip: If you feel discomfort, you can place a mat or towel underneath you. The band can be wrapped around any stable object if a power rack or pole is not available.
how_to: Wrap a band around a power rack or pole 1-2 feet above head level.
Position yourself on your knees in front of it while gripping either end of the band with an underhand grip at shoulder-level.
Exhale and curl your body forward while keeping your knees firmly in place on the ground and your hands at shoulder-level. Do not allow your arms to help you with the movement.
Continue curling your body forward until you are no longer able to do so without the help of your arms or your knees leaving the ground.
Inhale and allow your torso to straighten, returning to the starting position.

name: Kneeling Cable Crunch
pro_tip: If your knees hurt, try using a mat or other soft object like a towel to cushion them.
how_to: Kneel on the ground in front of a cable machine, holding one end of the rope in each hand around your face.
Exhale and bend your torso forward without moving your lower body.
Continue until you can no longer do so.
Inhale and allow your torso to be raised back up, returning to the starting position.

name: Kneeling Cable Tricep Extension
pro_tip: If your knees hurt, try using a mat or other soft object like a towel to cushion them.
how_to: Position yourself on your knees in front of a bench while holding a cable shoulder-width apart with an overhand grip.
While resting your upper arms on the bench, exhale and extend your arms to straighten them.
Continue until your arms are completely straight, keeping your upper arms on the bench and knees on the floor.
Inhale and allow your arms to bend back, returning to the starting position.

name: Kneeling Cobra Push Up
pro_tip: If your knees hurt, try using a mat or other soft object like a towel to cushion them.
how_to: Position yourself on the ground with knees bent and hands slightly wider than shoulder-width apart at the level of your chest.
Inhale and lower yourself towards the floor by leaning forward and allowing your elbows to bend.
As your chest almost touches the ground, arch your back upwards and begin to push up through your hands, exhaling.
Continue to arch backward and push through your hands until your arms are fully extended.
Inhale and begin lowering yourself while bending forward until your chest almost touches the ground.
Exhale and push forward with your hands to rock yourself back into the starting position.

name: Kneeling Decline Push Up
pro_tip: If you want to increase the difficulty of this movement, straighten your legs and place your feet on the box instead.
how_to: Position yourself with your knees bent and rested on a raised surface like a box while placing your hands shoulder-width apart at the level of your chest.
Exhale and press yourself up by extending your arms and pivoting at your knees.
Continue until your arms fully extend and straighten.
Inhale and allow your arms to bend, lowering yourself until just before your chest makes contact with the ground, returning to the starting position.

name: Kneeling Diamond Push
pro_tip: If your knees hurt, try using a mat or other soft object like a towel to cushion them.
how_to: Position yourself with your knees bent and rested on the ground while placing your hands in a diamond formation underneath your chest.
Exhale and raise yourself up by extending your arms and pivoting at your knee.
Continue until your arms are fully extended, while keeping your hips from dropping.
Inhale and allow your arms to bend, lowering yourself down and returning to the starting position.

name: Lat Pulldown
pro_tip: If your butt accidentally comes off the bench, you can adjust the pads or seat to make sure your thighs are secured properly.
how_to: Sit down on the bench while securing your thighs with the pads and gripping the bar overhead with an overhand grip much wider than shoulder-width apart.
Exhale and pull the bar downward, driving your elbows into your sides while simultaneously driving your shoulder blades down and together.
Continue lowering the bar until it is just above your shoulder level.
Inhale and allow your arms to raise overhead while your shoulder blades part to return to the starting position.

name: Lat Pulldown Machine
pro_tip: Do not pull the bar down further than your shoulder level.
how_to: Sit on the machine with your feet firmly planted on the ground, thighs secured by the pad, and hands placed on the handles with an overhand grip wider than shoulder-width apart.
Exhale and pull the bar down towards the ground by driving your elbows downwards and back while squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Continue pulling the bar down until it reaches about shoulder level.
Inhale and allow the bar to raise until your arms are fully extended, returning to the starting position.

name: Lateral Raise
pro_tip: For added benefit, hold the dumbbells for an extra 1 second before lowering them, when your arms are parallel to the floor.
how_to: Stand upright, holding both dumbbells by your sides with your arms extended.
Without using your legs, exhale and raise the dumbbells out to your sides.
Continue raising the dumbbells until your arms are parallel to the floor.
Inhale and allow the dumbbells to lower, returning them to the starting position.

name: Lateral Raise Machine
pro_tip: For added benefit, adjust the machine so that your hands start closer together.
how_to: Sit in the machine with your feet, butt, and lower back all firmly planted on the machine while you grip the handles.
Exhale and raise your arms out to the sides.
Continue raising your arms until they are parallel to the ground.
Inhale and lower your arms back down, returning to the starting position.

name: Leaning Overhead Rope Tricep Extension
pro_tip: The higher you keep your upper arms during this movement, the more you'll train the long head of your triceps.
how_to: Face away from the cable machine while gripping one end of the rope with either hand, staggering your feet, and bending forward with the rope held overhead.
Exhale and extend your arms forward in the direction your head is pointing.
Continue extending your arms until they are completely straight.
Inhale and allow your arms to bend, returning the rope behind your head in the starting position.

name: Leg Extension
pro_tip: To keep yourself firmly in the seat, try actively pulling yourself down towards it with the handles at your sides.
how_to: Sit down on the machine with your butt, lower back, and upper back firmly placed against it while you position your legs behind the pad.
Set up the machine's backrest, seat height, and pad position so that your feet are pointed directly towards the ground or slightly back, with the pad pressed against your lower shins.
Exhale and extend your legs, straightening them while holding onto the handles at your sides.
Continue extending your legs until they are completely straight.
Inhale and lower your legs, returning them to the starting position.

name: Leg Press
pro_tip: The further the machine goes, the greater the benefit. Adjust the safety mechanism accordingly.
how_to: Orient yourself on the machine, placing your butt, lower back, upper back, and head all firmly in the seat.
Adjust the safety mechanism to determine your desired range of motion, selecting one where your thighs make at least a 90º angle with your lower legs.
With your hands gripping the side bars, feet parallel to each other shoulder-width apart and toes pointed slightly outward, unlock the safety mechanism so that the machine can freely move.
Exhale, extending your legs forward and straightening them.
Continue to extend your legs while keeping all body parts firmly in the seat and your feet flatly pressed against the machine until your legs are straight.
Inhale and lower your legs down, allowing them to bend in order to return to the starting position.
Relock the safety mechanism to hold the machine in place so that you can safely exit.

name: Leg Press Calf Raise
pro_tip: For added benefit, lower your toes slowly on the way down.
how_to: Orient yourself on the machine, placing your butt, lower back, upper back, and head all firmly in the seat.
Adjust the safety mechanism to determine your desired range of motion, selecting the one where your legs are closest to being straight.

Grip the side bars, placing your feet parallel to each other shoulder-width apart with your toes pointed forward so that only the balls of your feet and your toes are in contact with the plate of the machine.
unlock the safety mechanism so that the machine can freely move.
Fully extend your legs until they are straight.
Exhale and press the machine forward by pushing through the balls of your feet and toes while keeping your legs straight.
When you can't go any further, inhale and bring your toes back down, returning to the starting position.
Bring your legs back and relock the safety mechanism to safely exit the machine.

name: Leg Press Machine
pro_tip: If you are flexible enough, starting the machine's plate even closer to you will have added benefit.
how_to: Orient yourself on the machine, placing your butt, lower back, upper back, and head all firmly in the seat.
Adjust the machine so that your thighs make at least a 90º angle with your lower legs.
With your hands gripping the side bars, feet parallel to each other shoulder-width apart and toes pointed slightly outward exhale and press forward, extending your legs.
Continue until your legs straighten out in front of you while making sure you stay firmly in the seat.
Inhale and draw your legs back, returning to the starting position.

name: Leg Raise
pro_tip: You can increase the difficulty of this movement by preventing your feet from touching the ground between reps.
how_to: Lie supine on the floor or a mat with your legs fully extended, arms straight, and head firmly planted.
Exhale and raise your legs up toward your torso while keeping them straight and the rest of your body firmly on the ground.
Continue raising your legs until your legs are pointed directly up.
Inhale and lower your legs down to the floor, returning to the starting position.

name: Low Bar Barbell Back Squat
pro_tip: Always keep a slight forward lean with a flat back while performing this movement to avoid dropping the barbell.
how_to: With feet shoulder-width apart, position yourself under the center of the barbell in the rack as you place it over your upper back, and grip the barbell slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.

While maintaining a slight forward lean, lift the barbell from the rack by partially standing up and taking a step back while squeezing the bar tightly and keeping it rested over your upper back, lower than a standard squat.
Inhale and break at your hips, sitting down and allowing your torso to come forward while keeping it straight.
Exhale and push through your heels to return to the starting position.
Continue until your thighs are at least parallel to the floor.
After all reps are completed, walk forward to return the barbell to the rack, continuing to maintain a slight forward lean.

name: Lying Crunch Machine
pro_tip: Forcefully exhaling while raising yourself up can increase the effectiveness of this movement.
how_to: Lie down on the machine with your feet placed on the rest and hands behind your head holding the handles.
Exhale and crunch yourself forward.
Continue until your elbow are several inches from your thighs.
Inhale and lower yourself down by allowing yourself to lean back.

name: Lying Dumbbell Tricep Extension
pro_tip: Make sure you always keep the dumbbells to the side of your head and don't accidentally raise them over your face.
how_to: Lie flat on the bench so that your head, upper back, lower back, and both feet are firmly pressed against the bench and ground at all points.
Raise two dumbbells to the level of your head with your palms facing toward each other, arms bent, and elbows tucked into your sides.
Exhale, extending your arms to raise the dumbbells overhead while keeping your elbows pointed forward.
Continue to extend your arms until they are straight.
Inhale, lowering the dumbbells to the starting position.

name: Lying Leg Curl
pro_tip: For added benefit, lower your legs slowly.
how_to: Lie face down, adjusting the machine so that the pad is between your calf and the back of your ankle while grabbing the handles in front of you.
Exhale as you curl your legs towards you, trying to bring the pad towards your butt.
While keeping your thighs firmly pressed against the machine, continue to curl your legs until you can no longer do so.
Inhale and lower your legs back down.

name: Lying Tricep Extension
pro_tip: If you do not have access to an EZ bar, you can substitute it for a barbell.
how_to: Lie flat on the bench so that your head, upper back, lower back, and both feet are firmly pressed against the bench and ground at all points while holding an EZ bar above your head with an overhand grip.
With elbows tucked in and bent, exhale and extend your arms so that you raise the EZ bar overhead.
Continue until your arms are fully extended.
Inhale and lower the EZ bar down without allowing your upper arm to move, returning to the starting position.

name: Medium Cable Chest Fly
pro_tip: Squeeze your chest while driving your arms forward and down for added benefit.
how_to: Stand between two cables positioned slightly above shoulder level, gripping them with your palms facing forward.
Exhale and bring your arms forward and down, keeping them straight.
Continue until just before your hands would touch.
Inhale and allow your arms to raise to your sides, returning to the starting position.

name: Mid Shin Stiff Legged Barbell Deadlift
pro_tip: Make sure to maintain a flat back above all else throughout the entire movement.
how_to: Place a barbell on the floor and position yourself over the center of it with your feet shoulder-width apart and shins about 1 inch away from the barbell.
Maintaining a straight back, bend down with your legs while leaning forward and position your hands on the barbell shoulder-width apart with an overhand grip and fully extended arms.
Exhale and push through your feet while extending your legs to begin lifting the barbell while maintaining a flat back until you stand upright to get into position to begin the movement.
Standing upright with your legs straight, lean forward while inhaling and maintaining a flat back.
Continue until the barbell reaches your mid shins.
Exhale and raise the barbell up by leaning back until your torso is in line with your lower body, returning to the starting position. Do not lean back further than this.

name: Narrow Grip Pull Up
pro_tip: Try to tighten your abs to keep your legs below you, preventing them from swinging as you pull yourself up.
how_to: Grab the bar with an overhand shoulder-width apart grip, with your arms fully extended and legs held straight below you.
Exhale and pull yourself up by tucking your elbows in and driving your shoulder blades down and together.
Continue pulling yourself up until your chin passes the bar.
Inhale and lower yourself down until your arms are straight again, returning to the starting position.

name: Narrow Squat On Book
pro_tip: Any sturdy flat item that can support your body weight and will not move can be used as a substitute item to perform this movement with.
how_to: Stand upright with your feet closer than shoulder-width apart, heels on a book, and hands on your hips.
Inhale and break at your hips, sitting down and allowing your torso to come forward while keeping it straight.
Continue lowering yourself until your thighs are at least parallel to the ground.
Exhale and raise yourself up by pushing through your heels until you return to the starting position.

name: Oblique Crunch
pro_tip: Try to avoid pulling on your head with your hand as it can cause discomfort in your neck later on.
how_to: Lie on your side with knees bent, one hand behind your head, and the other across your abdomen.
Exhale and bend upwards toward your side while keeping your hips and lower abdomen on the floor.
Continue to bend upwards toward your side until you can no longer do so.
Inhale and lower yourself to the ground, returning to the starting position.
After all reps are completed, switch sides and repeat the movement. 10 reps prescribed means you should perform 10 reps on each side (20 total)

name: Olympic Parallel Bar Hammer Curl
pro_tip: Lower the bar slowly for added benefit.
how_to: Stand upright with your feet shoulder-width apart and arms fully extended in front of your body with your palms facing one another.
Exhale and curl the bar up towards your shoulder while keeping your upper arm fixed at your side.
Continue curling the bar until it reaches about the level of your shoulder and you can no longer curl it higher while still keeping your upper arm by your side.
Inhale and lower the bar down, returning to the starting position.

name: One Arm Band Cross Body Chest Press
pro_tip: Standing farther away from where the band is tied to increase resistance. Stand closer to decreases resistance. The band can be wrapped around any stable object if a power rack or pole is not available.
how_to: Wrap a band around a power rack or pole at shoulder-level and stand upright with your feet shoulder-width apart, facing a direction perpendicular to the band.
With the arm closest to the band held at shoulder-level and bent, grip the band.
Exhale and press diagonally forward and inward across your body while keeping your arm at shoulder-level, not allowing its height to change or your torso to rotate.
Continue to press your arm diagonally until it is fully extended.
Inhale and allow your arm to bend back to the starting position, continuing to prevent your torso from rotating.
After all reps are completed, switch sides and repeat the movement. 10 reps prescribed means you should perform 10 reps on each side (20 total).

name: One Arm Band Lateral Raise
pro_tip: If you have the flexibility to do so, raise your arm several inches above shoulder-level. The band can be wrapped around any stable object if a power rack or pole is not available.
how_to: Wrap a band around the lowest portion of a power rack or pole.
Stand upright with one arm on your hip and the other fully extended by your side. Grip one end of the band with your palm facing inward.
Exhale and raise your arm up to your side, keeping it in line with the side of your body while maintaining the position of your torso.
Continue raising your arm until it is at least parallel to the ground.
Inhale and bring your arm back in towards your body, keeping it straight and returning to the starting position.
After all reps are completed, switch sides and repeat the movement. 10 reps prescribed means you should perform 10 reps on each side (20 total).

name: One Arm Band Leaning Overhead Tricep Extension Over Band
pro_tip: Try to keep your torso upright as best as you can. If you lean too far forward you will alter the mechanics of the movement.
how_to: Stand upright in a staggered stance, with your feet shoulder-width apart and a band securely positioned under your back foot.
Position your upper arm next to your head, bent, and gripping one end of the band with your palm facing away from you.
Hold your upper arm in place with your opposite arm and exhale, extending your arm overhead.
Keeping the upper portion of your arm still, continue until your arm straightens and is fully extended overhead.
Inhale and lower your arm, allowing it to bend and return to the starting position.
After all reps are completed, switch sides and repeat the movement. 10 reps prescribed means you should perform 10 reps on each side (20 total).

name: One Arm Cable Chest Fly
pro_tip: To increase lat involvement, set the handle up at a higher position.
how_to: Stand with feet slightly wider than shoulder-width apart facing perpendicular to the machine, with your arm outstretched, gripping the handle at shoulder level.
While bending slightly forward and keeping your arm straight exhale and swing your arm down across your body.
Continue until your arm reaches the level of your opposite hip.
Inhale and allow your arm to raise up and back, returning to the starting position.
After all reps are completed, switch sides and repeat the movement. 10 reps prescribed means you should perform 10 reps on each side (20 total).

name: One Arm Cable Curl
pro_tip: If the handle you select is uncomfortable to grip, you can always substitute it for a more comfortable one.
how_to: Stand upright facing the machine holding the cable at shoulder-width with an underhand grip and your other hand resting behind your back.
Exhale and curl the cable up in the direction of your shoulder, avoiding using your legs or back to lift, and keeping your upper arm by your side.
Continue curling the cable with your upper arm by your side until it reaches the level of your shoulder and you cannot curl it any further.
Inhale and lower the cable down, returning it to the starting position.
After all reps are completed, switch sides and repeat the movement. 10 reps prescribed means you should perform 10 reps on each side (20 total).

name: One Arm Cable Front Raise
pro_tip: Try to hold your arm in place at the top for 1 second each rep for added benefit.
how_to: Stand upright facing away from the machine with your feet shoulder-width apart and gripping the handle with an overhand grip in front of your hip at shoulder-width while your other hand is rested behind your back.
Exhale and raise your arm while keeping it straight.
Continue raising your arm until it becomes parallel with the ground.
Inhale and lower your arm, keeping it straight and returning to the starting position.
After all reps are completed, switch sides and repeat the movement. 10 reps prescribed means you should perform 10 reps on each side (20 total).

name: One Arm Cable Lateral Raise
pro_tip: Try to hold your arm in place at the top for 1 second each rep for added benefit.
how_to: Stand upright facing away from the machine with your feet shoulder-width apart and gripping the handle with an inwards facing palm in front of your hip at shoulder-width while your other hand is rested behind your back.
Exhale and raise your arm out to the side while keeping it straight.
Continue raising your arm until it is parallel with the ground.
Inhale and allow your arm to lower, returning it to the starting position.
After all reps are completed, switch sides and repeat the movement. 10 reps prescribed means you should perform 10 reps on each side (20 total).

name: One Arm Cable Seated Row
pro_tip: Keep your torso straight and prevent it from twisting by consciously tightening your abs.
how_to: Sit on a bench with a single arm outstretched in front of you just below the level of your shoulder gripping the handle at shoulder-width with an inwards facing palm.
Exhale and bring your arm back by driving your elbow behind you and keeping it tucked in.
Continue to pull your arm back, simultaneously driving your shoulder blade back as well until your elbow passes your torso.
Inhale and allow your arm to extend, returning to the starting position.
After all reps are completed, switch sides and repeat the movement. 10 reps prescribed means you should perform 10 reps on each side (20 total).

name: One Arm Cable Tricep Kickback
pro_tip: Focus on consciously squeezing your triceps for added benefit.
how_to: Stand facing the machine with a moderate forward lean and flat back while holding onto the cable with an inward facing palm and your arm bent.
Exhale and extend your arm to straighten it while keeping your upper arm still.
Continue while making sure your legs and torso do not move until your arm is straight.
Inhale and allow your arm to bend, returning it to the starting position.
After all reps are completed, switch sides and repeat the movement. 10 reps prescribed means you should perform 10 reps on each side (20 total).

name: One Arm Cable Underhand Tricep Extension
pro_tip: Try to consciously focus on squeezing your triceps while you press down for added benefit.
how_to: Stand upright with one hand behind your back and the other hand gripping the handle at shoulder-width with an underhand grip in front of your shoulder.
Exhale and extend your arm while keeping your upper arm in place.
Continue until your arm is straight.
Inhale and allow your arm to raise, returning it to the starting position.
After all reps are completed, switch sides and repeat the movement. 10 reps prescribed means you should perform 10 reps on each side (20 total).

name: One Arm Dumbbell Reverse Wrist Curl
pro_tip: Try to lower the dumbbell slowly to improve the effectiveness of the movement.
how_to: Sit on the edge of the bench while leaning forward with your forearm resting on your thigh, holding a dumbbell with an overhand grip.
Exhale and extend your hand upwards.
Continue to raise your hand while keeping your forearm on your thigh until you can no longer do so.
Inhale and slowly lower your hand down, returning to the starting position.
After all reps are completed, switch sides and repeat the movement. 10 reps prescribed means you should perform 10 reps on each side (20 total).

name: One Arm Dumbbell Wrist Curl
pro_tip: Try to lower the dumbbell slowly to improve the effectiveness of the movement.
how_to: Sit on the edge of the bench while leaning forward with your forearm resting on your thigh, holding a dumbbell with an underhand grip.
Exhale and flex your hand upward.
Continue to raise your hand while keeping your forearm on your thigh until you can no longer do so.
Inhale and slowly lower your hand down, returning it to the starting position.
After all reps are completed, switch sides and repeat the movement. 10 reps prescribed means you should perform 10 reps on each side (20 total).

name: One Arm Lat Pulldown
pro_tip: Prevent your torso from moving while you pull by consciously tightening your abs.
how_to: Sit on the machine with your butt and feet firmly planted while your thighs are secured by the pad and arms is extended overhead at shoulder-width.
With an overhand grip, exhale and drive your elbow down, tucking it into your side while rotating your palm inward.
Keeping your torso straight, continue to bring your elbow down until it is by your side while you simultaneously drive your shoulder blade down and back.
Inhale and allow your arm to raise, extending it overhead to return to the starting position.
After all reps are completed, switch sides and repeat the movement. 10 reps prescribed means you should perform 10 reps on each side (20 total).

name: One Arm Lying Dumbbell Tricep Extension
pro_tip: Make sure you keep your upper arm directly above your shoulder at all times.
how_to: Lie flat on the bench so that your head, upper back, lower back, and both feet are firmly pressed against the bench and ground at all points.
Holding a dumbbell with an overhand grip over your shoulder, support the arm that is lifting the dumbbell with your opposite hand.
Inhale and lower the dumbbell toward your opposite shoulder by bending your arm.
Continue until the dumbbell is just above your opposite shoulder while holding your upper arm in place with your opposite hand.
Exhale and raise the dumbbell by straightening your arm, returning to the starting position.
After all reps are completed, switch sides and repeat the movement. 10 reps prescribed means you should perform 10 reps on each side (20 total).

name: One Arm Tricep Extension
pro_tip: Take extra care to avoid accidentally hitting your head with the dumbbell on the way down.
how_to: Sit with your feet and butt firmly planted and one arm flexed behind your head holding a dumbbell.
With your other hand on your hip exhale and extend the dumbbell overhead, focusing on keeping your upper arm from moving.
Continue until your arm is straight and the dumbbell is overhead.
Inhale and allow your arm to bend, returning to the starting position.
After all reps are completed, switch sides and repeat the movement. 10 reps prescribed means you should perform 10 reps on each side (20 total).

name: One Arm Twisting Cable Floor Row
pro_tip: This can be performed on a bench as well.
how_to: Sit on the floor with your legs and arm fully extended in front of you with a forward lean while holding the handle with an inward facing palm at shoulder-level.
Exhale and drive your elbow and shoulder blade back while simultaneously twisting your torso.
Continue this motion until your elbow passes your torso.
Inhale and allow your torso to rotate in the opposite direction, extending your arm to return to the starting position.
After all reps are completed, switch sides and repeat the movement. 10 reps prescribed means you should perform 10 reps on each side (20 total).

name: Outer Dumbbell Curl
pro_tip: Focus on consciously squeezing your biceps while raising the dumbbells for added benefit.
how_to: Stand upright with your hands by the side of your body with palms facing inwards, holding one dumbbell in each hand with a neutral grip.
Keeping your upper arms by your side, exhale and raise the dumbbells up towards your shoulders by flexing your arms and simultaneously rotating your palms outward. Avoid using your legs or back.
Continue until your arms are fully flexed and the dumbbells cannot be curled any further.
Inhale and lower the dumbbells down, returning to the starting position.

name: Overhead Crunch Machine
pro_tip: Exhale deeply while crunching forward to improve the effectiveness of the movement.
how_to: Sit on the machine with your butt and lower back firmly planted, legs secured behind the pads, and hands holding onto the overhead handles.
Exhale and crunch forward, bringing your chest towards your knees and knees toward your chest.
Continue until you can no longer do so while keeping your butt in the seat.
Inhale, allowing your legs to lower and torso to lean back to return to the starting position.

name: Overhead Rope Tricep Extension
pro_tip: The higher your elbows are pointed when you start, the more you'll train the long rear head of your triceps.
how_to: Stand upright facing away from the machine while holding a rope with both hands behind your head.
Exhale and extend your arms overhead, straightening them out while keeping your upper arms still.
Continue until your arms are straight overhead.
Inhale and lower your hands back down behind your head, returning to the starting position.

name: Parallel Bar Straight Leg Raise Hold
pro_tip: The length of time you hold the position can increase as you get stronger.
how_to: Hold onto the handles by your sides while using the pads to support your forearms and keeping your legs straight below you.
Keeping your legs together, exhale and raise them until they are parallel with the ground.
Hold this position for several seconds.
Inhale and lower your legs down, returning to the starting position.

name: Parallel Bar Twisting Leg Raise
pro_tip: To increase the difficulty of this movement, hold your legs in place for several seconds when they are parallel to the ground.
how_to: Position yourself with your forearms rested on the pads, hands gripping the handles, and straight legs pointed below you towards the side.
Exhale and raise your legs up toward the middle of your body, while keeping them close together.
Continue until your legs are parallel to the ground and directly in front of your body.
Inhale and lower your legs, continuing to point them toward the opposite side, returning to the starting position but on the opposite side of your body.
Switch sides.

name: Plank
pro_tip: Remember to breathe rhythmically throughout the movement.
how_to: With your legs extended behind you, rest on your forearms so that your upper arms are directly below your shoulders.
Keep your torso straight and do not allow your hips to drop while maintaining this position for the desired duration.

name: Plate Curl
pro_tip: You can use plates of all sizes for this movement as long as you can grip them and hold on long enough to perform it.
how_to: Stand upright with arms fully extended gripping a plate closer than shoulder-width apart and with an overhand grip.
Exhale and curl your arms up towards your shoulders while keeping your upper arm by your side.
Continue until you can no longer do so while you still keep your upper arm by your side.
Inhale and lower the plate down, returning to the starting position.

name: Preacher Curl
pro_tip: For added benefit, squeeze your biceps consciously when lifting the barbell up.
how_to: Sit upright with your arms fully extended on the pad, gripping the EZ bar closer than shoulder-width apart with palms facing away from you.
Keeping your upper arms by your side, exhale and raise the EZ bar up towards your shoulders by flexing your arms.
Keeping your upper arms on the pad, exhale and raise the EZ bar up towards your shoulders by flexing your arms.
Continue until your arms are fully flexed and the EZ bar cannot be curled any further.
Lower the EZ bar, returning to the starting position.

name: Preacher Curl Machine
pro_tip: On most versions of this machine, you can adjust the seat so that you can comfortably rest your arms on the pad if needed.
how_to: Sit on the machine with your upper arms resting on the pad and hands gripping the handles with an underhand grip.
Exhale and curl the handles toward your shoulder while keeping your elbows firmly pressed into the pad.
Continue to curl until you reach about shoulder level.
Inhale and lower the handles, returning to the starting position.

name: Preacher Hammer Curl
pro_tip: If the dumbbells are too large and get stuck on the pad when your arms are extended, try adjusting the seat.
how_to: Sit on the seat with your upper arms resting on the pad and palms facing inwards, holding one dumbbell in each hand with a neutral grip.
Exhale and raise the dumbbells toward your shoulders by flexing your arm while keeping your upper arm still on the pad.
Continue until the dumbbells pass your shoulder level.
Inhale and lower the dumbbells, returning to the starting position.

name: Prone Incline Barbell Curl
pro_tip: You may need to ask a friend for assistance handing the barbell to you for you to begin the movement. This movement may not work on all decline benches. If yours does not allow you to perform the movement, try switching to an incline (adjustable) bench instead.
how_to: Lie prone on a bench, inclined while holding a barbell shoulder-width apart with an underhand grip.
Exhale and curl the barbell up towards your shoulders, while maintaining a neutral head position.
Continue raising the barbell while keeping your upper arms directly under your shoulders until you cannot curl it any longer.
Inhale and lower the barbell, returning it to the starting position.

name: Pull Up
pro_tip: If you want to increase the difficulty of this movement, hold a dumbbell between your feet by pressing them tightly together throughout the entire movement.
how_to: Grab the bar with an overhand grip much wider than shoulder-width apart while keeping your legs straight below you.
Exhale and pull yourself up toward the bar by bending your arms, driving your elbows down to your sides, and driving your shoulder blades down and together.
Continue until your chin passes the bar.
Inhale and allow yourself to lower your body down until your arms are fully extended, returning to the starting position.

name: Pull Up On Angled Bar
pro_tip: If you want to increase the difficulty of this movement, hold a dumbbell between your feet by pressing them tightly together throughout the entire movement.
how_to: Grab the bar with an overhand grip much wider than shoulder-width apart while keeping your legs bent and feet crossed.
Exhale and pull yourself up toward the bar by bending your arms, driving your elbows down to your sides, and driving your shoulder blades down and together.
Continue until your chin passes the bar.
Inhale and allow yourself to lower your body down until your arms are fully extended, returning to the starting position.

name: Push Up
pro_tip: Keep your abs tight if you are having trouble maintaining a straight torso.
how_to: Position yourself prone on the ground with your legs fully extended and hands positioned at the level of your chest slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.
Exhale and press yourself up by extending your arms while keeping your hips up and torso straight.
Continue until your arms are fully extended and straight.
Inhale and lower yourself down until just before your chest touches the floor, returning to the starting position.

name: Push Up With Back Extension
pro_tip: Do not allow your knees to make contact with the floor, while pressing yourself up.
how_to: Lie prone on the floor with your legs extended behind you and hands shoulder-width apart at the level of your chest.
Exhale and press yourself up through your hands to extend your arms while simultaneously raising your chest upwards by leaning back.
Continue to raise yourself until your arms are fully extended and you are leaning as far back as you can.
Inhale and lower yourself down by lowering your chest and bending your arms to return to the starting position.

name: Recumbent Bike
pro_tip: Remember to breathe rhythmically throughout the duration of this movement.
how_to: Sit on the bike with your butt, lower back, and upper back positioned firmly on the machine.
Select the appropriate settings on the machine for your planned cardio.
Press start.
Push one leg forward extending it while pulling the other towards your torso.
Repeat this motion rhythmically for the duration of your cardio.
Select the appropriate settings on the machine for your planned cardio.

name: Renegade Row
pro_tip: This is an advanced movement and may be difficult to perform.
how_to: Position yourself with two dumbbells slightly wider than shoulder-width apart at your chest level, with your legs extended behind you.
With your arms fully extended in push up position, inhale and lower yourself down until just before your chest touches the ground.
Exhale and then push yourself up until your arms are fully extended.
Row one dumbbell up, driving your elbow and shoulder blade back until it passes your torso.
Inhale and lower your arm down to place the dumbbell on the ground, returning to the starting position.
Switch sides.

name: Reverse Crunch
pro_tip: If you feel discomfort, you can place a mat underneath you.
how_to: Lie on the floor facing the ceiling with your legs bent and thighs raised directly above your hips.
Exhale and curl your knees toward your head, allowing your butt and lower back to come off the floor.
Continue until your knees pass over your upper chest.
Inhale and lower your legs, returning them to the starting position.

name: Reverse Fly Machine With Overhand Grip
pro_tip: To maximize benefit, start with the handle grips as close together as you can without experiencing discomfort in your shoulders. If the machine at your gym as set up for performing a regular chest fly, you can usually adjust the starting position of the handles to set yourself up for a reverse fly instead.
how_to: Sit on the machine with your chest firmly pressed against the pad, grabbing the handles at shoulder-level with an overhand grip.
Exhale and rotate your straight arms back around your body while squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Continue until your arms are in line with the sides of your body.
Inhale and bring your arms forward, returning to the starting position.

name: Reverse Fly Machine With Parallel Grip
pro_tip: To maximize benefit, start with the handle grips as close together as you can without experiencing discomfort in your shoulders. If the machine at your gym as set up for performing a regular chest fly, you can usually adjust the starting position of the handles to set yourself up for a reverse fly instead.
how_to: Sit on the machine with your chest firmly pressed against the pad, grabbing the handles at shoulder-level with a parallel grip.
Exhale and rotate your straight arms back around your body while squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Continue until your arms are in line with the sides of your body.
Inhale and bring your arms forward, returning to the starting position.

name: Reverse Hyper
pro_tip: Keep your legs pressed together during the movement.
how_to: Lie on a bench so that your hips are positioned above its edge with your legs fully extended behind you.
While grasping the bench, exhale and raise your legs.
Continue to raise your legs until they rise above the level of your torso.
Inhale and lower your legs, returning to the starting position.

name: Reverse Push Up
pro_tip: Try to avoid turning this movement into a crunch, focus on your back not your abs.
how_to: Lie on the ground with knees bent and bent arms positioned slightly below shoulder level.
Exhale and push through your elbows, focusing on squeezing your shoulder blades together and bringing your elbows toward one another while raising your chest slightly.
Continue until your shoulder blades are fully squeezed.
Inhale and lower yourself down, returning to the starting position.

name: Reverse Push Up On Chair
pro_tip: Make sure your elbows aren't positioned on the very edge of the chairs to minimize fall risk.
how_to: Lie with your knees bent and bent arms positioned slightly below shoulder level on the chairs.
Exhale and drive your elbows down into the chairs, bringing your elbows in toward each other to raise your torso up, squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Continue raising yourself up until your elbows pass behind your torso.
Inhale and lower yourself back down, returning to the starting position.

name: Rope Crunch
pro_tip: Exhale very deeply while crunching down to maximize the benefits of this movement.
how_to: Stand upright facing away from the machine while gripping a rope above your head with bent arms.
Maintaining your arm angle and straight legs, curl your chest down toward your waist.
Continue curling yourself until your head reaches the level of your waist.
Inhale and allow yourself to rise back up, returning to the starting position.

name: Rope Extension
pro_tip: To emphasize the lateral head of your triceps even more, tuck your elbows a little further back.
how_to: Stand upright while facing the machine and gripping the rope attachment with your upper arms by your sides and arms bent.
With your elbows tucked by your side, exhale and press the rope downward extending your arms.
Continue to press down while keeping your upper arms still until your arms are fully extended.
Inhale and raise the rope, returning to the starting position.

name: Rope Face Pull
pro_tip: If you have the flexibility to do so, you can bring the rope back even further until the point that your upper arms pass behind your torso.
how_to: Stand upright while facing the machine with your arms extended in front of you above shoulder-level while grasping the rope.
Exhale and bring the rope back and down toward your chest while driving your elbows back and squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Continue until your upper arms are at least in line with your torso.
Inhale and allow your arms to extend again, raising the rope above.
